1	# Architecture Decision Records
2	
3	Short, dated records of _architectural_ decisions — ones that shape system structure, boundaries, or contracts other code depends on. Not a changelog, not a design doc, not a place to explain what the code does — comments and `ARCHITECTURE.md` already do that.
4	
5	## Index
6	
7	One line per ADR, with what it guards. Add a line when you add an ADR.
8	
9	- [1. Parse with OXC instead of the TypeScript compiler](0001-oxc-over-typescript-compiler.md) — do not add a type-checking pass to the default path. The opt-in backend is 0006.
10	- [2. Hand-write Serialize/Deserialize for PropType instead of deriving it](0002-manual-serialize-for-prop-type.md) — do not derive them on `PropType` or `CollectedType`.
11	- [3. Cache the DTS parse cache with positional (not named) MessagePack](0003-positional-msgpack-cache-encoding.md) — do not reorder, insert or remove `SourceData` fields without bumping `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION`.
12	- 4. Defer full type-checker integration — removed: superseded by 0006. The gap list and gates are in `docs/type-checker-integration.md`.
13	- [5. Contain panics at a single, per-item boundary](0005-panic-containment-boundary.md) — route anything reachable from a rayon `.map()`, a `DocgenPlugin` hook or a NAPI entry point through `contain_panic`.
14	- [6. Run the TypeScript backend as a second resolver](0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md) — do not patch `Opaque` leaves, give `crates/core` a compiler process or I/O, or route the backend through NAPI.
15	
16	- [7. Let the backend discover components, always compile it in, and keep structural as the default](0007-backend-discovers-components-and-compiles-in.md) — do not feature-gate the backend crate, run it by default, or let it replace a structural entry on a clash.
17	- [8. Discard the parse cache whenever the build that wrote it differs](0008-parse-cache-keyed-by-build.md) — do not load cache entries without checking the payload's header against the running build.
18	- [9. Write each distinct prop once in the canonical output](0009-canonical-output-interns-props.md) — do not inline props in canonical JSON or derive prop ids from position.
19	- [10. Load dependency declarations by name, before resolution, into a shared layer](0010-load-dependency-declarations-by-name.md) — do not load dependency files by import closure, resolve against them lazily during resolution, or emit their components or enums. Its precedence of shortcuts over dependency declarations is superseded by 0014.
20	- [11. Find dependency declarations through a per-package export index, not the parse cache](0011-per-package-export-index.md) — do not put dependency files in the `DtsCache` or reuse an index whose package's `package.json` changed.
21	- [12. Collapse large inherited dependency sources, as Storybook does](0012-collapse-large-dependency-sources.md) — do not resolve a collapsed source's props, or collapse a component's own props.
22	- [13. Read React's attribute declarations in curated mode, in an index of their own](0013-curated-mode-reads-react-attributes-apart.md) — do not merge React into the project index outside Full mode, or make the React index a lookup fallback.
23	- [14. A loaded declaration wins over a known shortcut; shortcuts are fallbacks](0014-declarations-before-shortcuts.md) — do not check a shortcut before a declaration, or add one without measuring it against the declaration on consumer code.
24	- 15. A member read through React's types reads React's declaration and what it imports — removed: a resolver behavior, not a structure. It lives in `docs/architecture/resolver-type-resolution.md` ("Member reads through React's types").
25	- [16. Resolve components on request, and load dependencies for the names their resolution reaches](0016-resolve-components-on-request.md) — do not make a lazy answer differ from batch extraction's for the same key, memoize a resolution that found a dependency name missing, or expose a parser type from the session API. Extends 0010's loading from "before resolution" to "before the resolution that answers".
26	- [17. Version the canonical JSON, and make readers reject a version they don't read](0017-version-the-canonical-json.md) — do not change the canonical JSON's shape without bumping `SCHEMA_VERSION`, or let a reader accept a version it was not written for.
27	- [18. Write prop sets and name lists once in the canonical output](0018-canonical-output-interns-prop-sets-and-name-lists.md) — do not write a component's props, an inheritance layer's `omitted` or a diagnostic's `affects` inline in canonical JSON. Extends 0009's per-prop table to the lists that repeat across components; `SCHEMA_VERSION` 2.
28	- [19. Load dependency declarations by default](0019-load-dependencies-by-default.md) — do not make a surface default `loadDependencies` to off, or compare a baseline recorded without a flag against a build with the other default. Supersedes 0010's "off by default".
29	- 20. Chain dependency layers and load the remaining names after three growths — removed: a tuning of 0016's design with measurements, not a new decision. It lives in `docs/architecture/pipeline-orchestration.md` ("Demand-driven dependencies") and `docs/performance.md`. It replaced 0016's 48-growth threshold.
30	- [21. Publish the semantic backend crates with the CLI](0021-publish-the-semantic-backend-crates.md) — keep the runtime opt-in backend available in the published CLI by releasing its versioned crate dependencies first.
31	- [22. Ask a warm checker for the requested component](0022-ask-a-warm-checker-for-the-requested-component.md) — do not route by predicted risk or check the whole project to answer one story: ask the TypeScript checker for the component a request names, wait a bounded time, and take the structural answer when it is slower. Extends 0007's runtime opt-in from a project run to a session.
32	- [23. Function parameters carry `optional` and `rest`](0023-function-parameters-carry-optional-and-rest.md) — do not print a function type without its `?` and `...` parameters, or add a parameter flag without a `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump and a reader update. `SCHEMA_VERSION` 3.
33	- [24. List every HTML attribute React declares by default](0024-list-every-html-attribute-by-default.md) — do not make `curated` the default `htmlAttributes`, or omit a prop `@types/react` declares. Supersedes 0013's default
34	
35	Changing any of these needs a new ADR. A removed entry keeps its number; its rationale moved to the doc named on its line.
36	
37	## When to write one
38	
39	Two gates, both required:
40	
41	1. **Architectural.** It affects one of: system structure (module/crate boundaries, how components interact), a dependency or technology choice that ripples across the codebase, a data format or contract other code depends on, or a cross-cutting constraint (performance model, correctness discipline, security model).
42	2. **Expensive to reverse and not obvious from the code.** If it gets reverted in a year, what breaks, and would anyone know why?
43	
44	If either answer is no, it's not an ADR.
45	
46	Good candidates:
47	
48	- Choosing OXC over the TypeScript compiler — a technology choice that shapes the whole extraction pipeline
49	- A serialization format with a hidden constraint (msgpack's positional encoding) — a data contract other code depends on
50	- Dropping a dependency, or an approach that was tried and abandoned
51	
52	Not ADR material:
53	
54	- A default, threshold or resolution order that one module reads (a collapse limit, a growth count, which lookup goes first) — that's a code comment plus the subsystem's `docs/architecture/` page. Measurements belong in `docs/performance.md`.
55	- A release or CI procedure (what to publish first, which gate blocks) — that's the workflow file.
56	- A superseded or tuned earlier decision whose design still holds — update the architecture page, don't stack a new ADR on it. Write one only if the contract itself changes.
57	- A single function's algorithm choice, confined to that function — that's a code comment
58	- A bug fix — commit message, and if it's the kind of thing that could recur, a line in `rdt-coverage.md`
59	- A behavior-preserving refactor — commit message is enough
60	- A naming or style convention — that's `AGENTS.md` or a lint rule
61	- Anything already obvious from the code or from `AGENTS.md`'s non-negotiables
62	- Per-user preferences, workflow notes and tool quirks — that's agent memory
63	
64	## Format
65	
66	One file per decision: `docs/adr/NNNN-short-title.md`, numbered sequentially, never reused. Copy `0000-template.md` to start.
67	
68	- **Never edit history.** If a decision changes, write a new ADR and mark the old one's status `Superseded by 000X`. Don't rewrite the old file to look like you knew all along.
69	- **Status** is one of: `Accepted`, `Superseded by NNNN`, `Deprecated`.
70	- Keep it short. If the technical depth doesn't fit on a screen, split it into its own doc and link it — see `0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md` pointing at `type-checker-integration.md` instead of inlining it.
71	
72	## Writing it
73	
74	Write like you're explaining it to the next engineer over their shoulder, not presenting it to a committee. Don't hard-wrap paragraphs at a fixed column — one line per paragraph, let the editor soft-wrap. Every other doc in this repo already does this; hard-wrapping just makes future diffs noisy when a sentence gets edited.
75	
76	**Cut the filler.** If a sentence still means the same thing without a word, delete the word.
77	
78	| Instead of | Write |
79	| --- | --- |
80	| "It's worth noting that this decision was made in order to leverage OXC's robust parsing capabilities" | "OXC parses in parallel with no type-checking pass" |
81	| "This represents a significant improvement in performance" | "32ms instead of several seconds" |
82	| "We decided to essentially utilize a positional encoding approach" | "We use positional encoding" |
83	| "In conclusion, this architecture provides a solid foundation going forward" | (delete — you already said the thing) |
84	
85	**Banned by default:** _leverage, utilize, robust, seamless, cutting-edge, essentially, basically, in order to, it's worth noting, it is important to note, at the end of the day._ If one is genuinely the precise technical word for something, fine — but check first.
86	
87	**Concrete beats vague.** Name the file, the number, the benchmark. "Slow" is not a fact; "several seconds on a mid-size design system" is.
88	
89	**Active voice, plain structure.** "We chose X because Y" beats "X was chosen due to Y considerations." Sentence-case headers, not Title Case.
90	
91	**Show the trade-off, not just the win.** A decision with no downside isn't a decision, it's a fact. Say what it costs.
92	
93	**Structure isn't fixed.** A paragraph, a paragraph plus bullets, a short table — whatever makes it scannable in one pass. `0006`'s Decision section is an intro line plus three bullets because it's three real choices; don't force that into one paragraph, and don't add sections or padding a one-line decision doesn't need.
94	
95	## What good looks like
96	
97	Read `0002-manual-serialize-for-prop-type.md` — a real bug behind it, a real number (`recursion_limit = 2048`), a real consequence, four sections, no throat-clearing.
98

- [12. Collapse large inherited dependency sources, as Storybook does](0012-collapse-large-dependency-sources.md) — do not resolve a collapsed source's props, or collapse a component's own props.
- [13. Read React's attribute declarations in curated mode, in an index of their own](0013-curated-mode-reads-react-attributes-apart.md) — do not merge React into the project index outside Full mode, or make the React index a lookup fallback.
- [14. A loaded declaration wins over a known shortcut; shortcuts are fallbacks](0014-declarations-before-shortcuts.md) — do not check a shortcut before a declaration, or add one without measuring it against the declaration on consumer code.
- 15. A member read through React's types reads React's declaration and what it imports — removed: a resolver behavior, not a structure. It lives in `docs/architecture/resolver-type-resolution.md` ("Member reads through React's types").
- [16. Resolve components on request, and load dependencies for the names their resolution reaches](0016-resolve-components-on-request.md) — do not make a lazy answer differ from batch extraction's for the same key, memoize a resolution that found a dependency name missing, or expose a parser type from the session API. Extends 0010's loading from "before resolution" to "before the resolution that answers".
- [17. Version the canonical JSON, and make readers reject a version they don't read](0017-version-the-canonical-json.md) — do not change the canonical JSON's shape without bumping `SCHEMA_VERSION`, or let a reader accept a version it was not written for.
- [18. Write prop sets and name lists once in the canonical output](0018-canonical-output-interns-prop-sets-and-name-lists.md) — do not write a component's props, an inheritance layer's `omitted` or a diagnostic's `affects` inline in canonical JSON. Extends 0009's per-prop table to the lists that repeat across components; `SCHEMA_VERSION` 2.
- [19. Load dependency declarations by default](0019-load-dependencies-by-default.md) — do not make a surface default `loadDependencies` to off, or compare a baseline recorded without a flag against a build with the other default. Supersedes 0010's "off by default".
- 20. Chain dependency layers and load the remaining names after three growths — removed: a tuning of 0016's design with measurements, not a new decision. It lives in `docs/architecture/pipeline-orchestration.md` ("Demand-driven dependencies") and `docs/performance.md`. It replaced 0016's 48-growth threshold.
- [21. Publish the semantic backend crates with the CLI](0021-publish-the-semantic-backend-crates.md) — keep the runtime opt-in backend available in the published CLI by releasing its versioned crate dependencies first.
- [22. Ask a warm checker for the requested component](0022-ask-a-warm-checker-for-the-requested-component.md) — do not route by predicted risk or check the whole project to answer one story: ask the TypeScript checker for the component a request names, wait a bounded time, and take the structural answer when it is slower. Extends 0007's runtime opt-in from a project run to a session.
- [23. Function parameters carry `optional` and `rest`](0023-function-parameters-carry-optional-and-rest.md) — do not print a function type without its `?` and `...` parameters, or add a parameter flag without a `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump and a reader update. `SCHEMA_VERSION` 3.
- [24. List every HTML attribute React declares by default](0024-list-every-html-attribute-by-default.md) — do not make `curated` the default `htmlAttributes`, or omit a prop `@types/react` declares. Supersedes 0013's default

Changing any of these needs a new ADR. A removed entry keeps its number; its rationale moved to the doc named on its line.

## When to write one

Two gates, both required:

1. **Architectural.** It affects one of: system structure (module/crate boundaries, how components interact), a dependency or technology choice that ripples across the codebase, a data format or contract other code depends on, or a cross-cutting constraint (performance model, correctness discipline, security model).
2. **Expensive to reverse and not obvious from the code.** If it gets reverted in a year, what breaks, and would anyone know why?

If either answer is no, it's not an ADR.

Good candidates:

- Choosing OXC over the TypeScript compiler — a technology choice that shapes the whole extraction pipeline
- A serialization format with a hidden constraint (msgpack's positional encoding) — a data contract other code depends on
- Dropping a dependency, or an approach that was tried and abandoned

Not ADR material:

- A default, threshold or resolution order that one module reads (a collapse limit, a growth count, which lookup goes first) — that's a code comment plus the subsystem's `docs/architecture/` page. Measurements belong in `docs/performance.md`.
- A release or CI procedure (what to publish first, which gate blocks) — that's the workflow file.
- A superseded or tuned earlier decision whose design still holds — update the architecture page, don't stack a new ADR on it. Write one only if the contract itself changes.
- A single function's algorithm choice, confined to that function — that's a code comment
- A bug fix — commit message, and if it's the kind of thing that could recur, a line in `rdt-coverage.md`
- A behavior-preserving refactor — commit message is enough
- A naming or style convention — that's `AGENTS.md` or a lint rule
- Anything already obvious from the code or from `AGENTS.md`'s non-negotiables
- Per-user preferences, workflow notes and tool quirks — that's agent memory

## Format

One file per decision: `docs/adr/NNNN-short-title.md`, numbered sequentially, never reused. Copy `0000-template.md` to start.

- **Never edit history.** If a decision changes, write a new ADR and mark the old one's status `Superseded by 000X`. Don't rewrite the old file to look like you knew all along.
- **Status** is one of: `Accepted`, `Superseded by NNNN`, `Deprecated`.
- Keep it short. If the technical depth doesn't fit on a screen, split it into its own doc and link it — see `0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md` pointing at `type-checker-integration.md` instead of inlining it.

## Writing it

Write like you're explaining it to the next engineer over their shoulder, not presenting it to a committee. Don't hard-wrap paragraphs at a fixed column — one line per paragraph, let the editor soft-wrap. Every other doc in this repo already does this; hard-wrapping just makes future diffs noisy when a sentence gets edited.

**Cut the filler.** If a sentence still means the same thing without a word, delete the word.

| Instead of | Write |
| --- | --- |
| "It's worth noting that this decision was made in order to leverage OXC's robust parsing capabilities" | "OXC parses in parallel with no type-checking pass" |
| "This represents a significant improvement in performance" | "32ms instead of several seconds" |
| "We decided to essentially utilize a positional encoding approach" | "We use positional encoding" |
| "In conclusion, this architecture provides a solid foundation going forward" | (delete — you already said the thing) |

**Banned by default:** _leverage, utilize, robust, seamless, cutting-edge, essentially, basically, in order to, it's worth noting, it is important to note, at the end of the day._ If one is genuinely the precise technical word for something, fine — but check first.

**Concrete beats vague.** Name the file, the number, the benchmark. "Slow" is not a fact; "several seconds on a mid-size design system" is.

**Active voice, plain structure.** "We chose X because Y" beats "X was chosen due to Y considerations." Sentence-case headers, not Title Case.

**Show the trade-off, not just the win.** A decision with no downside isn't a decision, it's a fact. Say what it costs.

**Structure isn't fixed.** A paragraph, a paragraph plus bullets, a short table — whatever makes it scannable in one pass. `0006`'s Decision section is an intro line plus three bullets because it's three real choices; don't force that into one paragraph, and don't add sections or padding a one-line decision doesn't need.

## What good looks like

Read `0002-manual-serialize-for-prop-type.md` — a real bug behind it, a real number (`recursion_limit = 2048`), a real consequence, four sections, no throat-clearing.

1	# 0008. Discard the parse cache whenever the build that wrote it differs
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-21
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	Under 0003 the cache is discarded only when someone bumps `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION`. Extractor changes that keep `SourceData`'s shape but change its content for the same input (#54, #69) were never bumped, so cached `.d.ts` results stayed stale with no signal. The version also lived only in `manifest.json`, a separate file from the payload, so two tool versions sharing a cache directory could pair one's manifest with the other's data.
8	
9	## Decision
10	
11	The payload starts with a header: schema version, crate version, and a fingerprint `build.rs` computes from the crate's sources and, in a workspace build, `Cargo.lock`. Loading decodes the header first and discards the cache unless all three match the running build. The manifest repeats the header for inspection only.
12	
13	- A cache from another build is discarded silently: that is the expected state after any upgrade.
14	- A cache from this build that fails to decode is discarded with an `Info` diagnostic.
15	- `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` still moves when `SourceData`'s shape changes, as 0003 says; the golden test pins that.
16	
17	## Consequences
18	
19	- Any code or dependency change invalidates the cache, including in development, with no step to remember.
20	- A cache never survives an upgrade, even one that changed nothing the cache depends on. The cache saves little time per run, so this costs little.
21	- Builds from the published crate fingerprint the crate's sources without `Cargo.lock`; the crate version covers the dependency set there.

1	# 0011. Find dependency declarations through a per-package export index, not the parse cache
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-23
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	Following a name from a package's entry point to the file that declares it walks re-export chains: chakra's `@ark-ui/react` is 1,434 mostly one-line `.d.mts` re-export files, and shadcn's icon packages re-export 1,500+ names each. Each hop is a file open and a resolver call, and opening files is the cost (0010). The msgpack `DtsCache` (0003, 0008) stores whole parsed files; measured on the dependency closures, a warm run was no faster than re-parsing in 6 of 7 cases (antd 80 ms warm against 45 ms with no cache), loading the cache alone cost 11–40 ms, and its 5,000-entry cap thrashed on shadcn's 6,217 files.
8	
9	## Decision
10	
11	The loader keeps a per-package export index next to the parse cache, and does not put dependency files in the `DtsCache`.
12	
13	- **Contents:** for each package entry module the loader looked up, its re-export graph flattened to exported name → (declaring file, local name), including `export *`, `export { a as b } from`, `export * as ns` and `import x; export { x }`; a name exported across a package boundary points into the other package's index. Modules whose exports are all their own declarations are not stored.
14	- **Keying and validation:** one file per package, keyed by the package's real path and a hash of the resolver configuration (tsconfig path and mtime, conditions). It is reused only while the package's `package.json` has the same mtime and size, and discarded with the rest of the cache when the build changes (0008).
15	- **Declaring files are parsed each run.** Parsing is cheap (418 MB/s); with the index, a warm run opens only the files that declare a loaded name.
16	
17	## Consequences
18	
19	- Warm runs open no re-export stub: resolver calls inside dependencies fell from 4,842 to 603 on shadcn and from 2,171 to 572 on chakra in the prototype, and loading cost 2–29 ms on the five projects.
20	- A package edited in place without touching `package.json` (patch-package) keeps a stale index until the cache is cleared.
21	- The index is written after loading; a cold run pays 10–55 ms more than a warm one.
22

1	# 0012. Collapse large inherited dependency sources, as Storybook does
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-23
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	With dependency declarations loaded (0010), a component inherits every prop of the package types it extends: a Radix primitive's handful, but also hundreds of style props. In chakra's own repository the prop count went from 560 to 398,910 (about 665 per component). Storybook 11's react-component-meta resolves everything and then hides a source from `node_modules` (or a `.d.ts`) that contributes more than 30 props, and React's `Attributes`/`RefAttributes`; RDT's default filter hides every prop declared in `node_modules`. Both resolve before they filter; skipping the resolution is where the time and memory go.
8	
9	## Decision
10	
11	`collapseInheritedProps: "dependencies" | "all" | "none"`, default `"dependencies"`, threshold 30, applied before resolving an inherited source.
12	
13	- **`"dependencies"`:** an inherited interface or alias declared in a dependency that contributes more than 30 props is not expanded. The component records it as an `InheritedLayer` with its `total_props`, and keeps only the curated notable props, as HTML attributes already work. Smaller dependency sources (`asChild`, `side`, `align`) are expanded into `props`.
14	- **`"all"`:** the same rule for project-declared sources too.
15	- **`"none"`:** expand everything, as RDT does before its filter.
16	- A component's own declared props are never collapsed.
17	
18	## Consequences
19	
20	- Default output matches what Storybook 11 shows: in an app that uses chakra or Mantine their style props collapse; in the design system's own repository, where they are project sources, they are listed.
21	- The design system's own repository keeps its large prop sets by default; sharing resolved props instead of copying them keeps that affordable (chakra with the experiment's loader: 2.1 s and 3.0 GB copied, 377 ms and 1.3 GB shared).
22	- A consumer that wants every prop sets `"none"` and pays the expansion.
23

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-23

## Context

1	# 0013. Read React's attribute declarations in curated mode, in an index of their own
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-23
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	When two members of an intersection declare the same prop, TypeScript intersects both types (#122). An HTML layer such as `ComponentProps<"div">` lists none of its element's attributes, yet declares them all, so a library prop named like a DOM attribute (recharts' `onTimeUpdate`) has the attribute's type as well. Only Full mode merged `@types/react`, so curated mode, which the CLI, the Vite plugin and Storybook use by default, showed the library's type alone. Merging React into the project index, as Full mode does, would also resolve every other React name in curated output (`ReactNode`, `CSSProperties`, the handler aliases) against the real declarations and change far more than these collisions.
8	
9	## Decision
10	
11	In curated mode, the cold run parses `@types/react` (through the parse cache) into its own `NamedTypeIndex`, held by the revision and passed to `ResolutionContext::with_react_types`. Only the HTML-layer attribute lookup (`resolver/html.rs`, via `ResolutionContext::react_index`) reads it. It is not a fallback of the project index, so no other lookup sees React's declarations. Full mode keeps merging React into the project index; `none` mode and the dependency loader (0010) don't read React at all.
12	
13	## Consequences
14	
15	- A prop that collides with an attribute of the layer's element has both types in curated mode too, with both declarations listed. The attribute keeps its alias name (`ReactEventHandler<HTMLDivElement>`), because nothing else in curated mode expands React's aliases.
16	- One more declaration file per run: `dtsFilesParsed` rises by one in every fixture snapshot. Wall time on the five benchmark corpora is unchanged within run-to-run noise.
17	- On those corpora with default flags, 7 shadcn props change (`ChartContainer.children` now intersects React's `children`); nothing else does.
18	- Without `@types/react`, curated mode behaves as before and reports nothing, since it never required it.
19

1	# 0014. A loaded declaration wins over a known shortcut; shortcuts are fallbacks
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-23
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	`known.rs` resolves library types by name (`HTMLChakraProps`, `SxProps`, cva's `VariantProps`, …) because the structural resolver couldn't expand their declarations. ADR 0010 kept that order for loaded dependencies: a project declaration, then a shortcut, then the dependency's own declaration. Measured against react-docgen-typescript on a consumer app with Chakra, MUI, Mantine, cva and react-aria-components installed, the loaded declarations now beat the shortcuts: Chakra's `HTMLChakraProps` gives 139 of RDT's props instead of 1, its `ButtonProps` 146 instead of 0, and Mantine's `StylesApiProps` 8 instead of 3. Only cva's `VariantProps`, which needs inference (`Parameters<C>[0]`), still needs its shortcut.
8	
9	## Decision
10	
11	- **Order:** a declaration, the project's or a loaded dependency's, then a known shortcut, then a React builtin (`resolver/precedence.rs`).
12	- **Fallback:** at the props-chain level, a declaration that evaluates to nothing (no props, no inherited layer, something left unevaluated) gives way to a shortcut of the same name, if one exists (`chain::known_fallback`). Its diagnostics are dropped with it.
13	- **Shortcuts kept:** only where the fallback measurably beats an unresolved name: the variant-props family, react-aria's `RenderProps`/`SlotProps`, and `HTMLChakraProps`/`HTMLArkProps`/`HTMLStyledProps` (an HTML layer when the package isn't loaded), plus React's own `PropsWithChildren`, `ComponentProps` and the like.
14	- **Shortcuts removed:** `SxProps`/`SystemStyleObject`/`SystemCssProperties` (printed worse text than the name itself), `OverridableStringUnion`, `ThemingProps`, `StylesApiProps` (opaque placeholders a loaded declaration beats), and the no-op `MantineColor`/`MantineSize`/`MantineRadius` arm.
15	
16	## Consequences
17	
18	- With `--load-dependencies`, a consumer of a component library gets the library's real props. Without it, a removed shortcut's name stays an unresolved named reference with the usual warning, as any other uninstalled package's type does; `PropType::SxProps` is no longer produced.
19	- A new shortcut needs the same evidence: it must beat the declaration, or stand in where the declaration can't be read, on code that uses the library.
20	- Library repos are unaffected: their own declarations already won (no change on the five benchmark corpora).
21

# 0010. Load dependency declarations by name, before resolution, into a shared layer

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-23

## Context

The pipeline parses only the project's own files, `@types/react` (full HTML-attribute mode) and TypeScript's lib files. An import into `node_modules` resolves to a path, but nothing parses that file, so a prop typed by a package (`ClosableType`, `OnValueChange`, a Radix primitive's props) stays an unresolved name. With dependencies installed, unresolved types sat at 116 (antd), 323 (chakra), 586 (spectrum) and about 1,000 (shadcn), and RDT expanded what we couldn't.

Loading whole files along imports is the wrong unit. The file-level closures of the five benchmark projects hold 150–6,218 files, and the cost is the file count: about 25 µs per file, almost all of it opening the file (18 threads open only 1.7× faster than one on macOS), against 418 MB/s for parsing. A prototype that loads only the files declaring a name the project uses read 39–833 files warm instead of 150–6,218.

## Decision

Behind `PipelineOptions::load_dependencies` (off by default here; on by default since [0019](0019-load-dependencies-by-default.md)), a phase before `NamedTypeIndex::build` loads the dependency declarations the project's type positions name, transitively, and nothing else.

- **Demands, not files.** A demand is a package specifier and an imported name used in a type position (a type reference, `typeof X`, heritage, a type argument). A loaded declaration's own references become new demands. One rayon scope runs them; each declaring file is claimed once, and results are keyed by file and name, so the outcome does not depend on scheduling.
- **A separate, shared layer.** Loaded declarations live in a `DependencyLayer` behind an `Arc`, with its own type index and import map. Project lookups fall back to it; keys are file paths, so the layers never collide. Watch revisions share it; an edit that adds a demand gets a new layer version with the new declarations added, never a copy of the project's data.
- **Precedence:** project declaration, then a known shortcut (`VariantProps`, `SxProps`, `HTMLChakraProps`, …), then a dependency declaration, then a builtin. The shortcuts exist because the real declarations are conditional types the structural resolver can't evaluate; a loaded declaration must not replace them.
- **Values stay out of the output.** A dependency's components go into a value index that `ComponentProps<typeof X>` and `typeof Pkg.Root` consult; they are never emitted. Dependency enums never become public output enums or feed the bare-name enum index.
- **Every unresolved demand is reported** on the component whose resolution reached it: a package with no types, an unresolvable specifier, a name the package doesn't export.

## Consequences

- In the experiment that proved this design (`exp/dependency-types`), unresolved types fell to 8 (mantine), 26 (chakra), 82 (shadcn), 58 (antd) and 172 (spectrum), for 2–29 ms of loading on a warm index.
- Props that reach large shared types grow sharply (chakra 560 → 398,910 in its own repo), which is why 0012 collapses large dependency sources and why resolved props are shared, not copied (#105).
- A watch edit that adds a package import costs one index lookup and a few files (under 1 ms in the prototype); `node_modules`, `package.json` and tsconfig changes still need `rebuild()`.
- `declare module` augmentations, `declare global` and `node:*` ambient modules are not loaded yet; a name only they provide stays unresolved, with a diagnostic.
- The TypeScript backend (0006, 0007) gets fewer incomplete components to handle; both now report parents inside `node_modules`.

By default the declarations those names point to are loaded (ADR 0010, on by default since ADR 0019): a prop typed by an installed package resolves. `--no-load-dependencies` (config, NAPI and Vite `loadDependencies: false`) reads only `@types/react` and TypeScript's own lib files from `node_modules`, and then a prop whose type comes from any other installed package stays a named reference with an `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT` warning. A declaration path that does not exist counts as none, so an unbuilt workspace package is reported as unresolved instead of resolving to a missing file. 26 27 **Invariant:** never build an `oxc_resolver::Resolver` for module resolution outside `ModuleResolvers`; a second configuration would resolve the same import to a different file. 28 29 ## Dependency declarations (`load_dependencies`, ADR 0010) 30 31 With `PipelineOptions::load_dependencies`, `ResolutionContext::with_dependencies` attaches the run's `DependencyLayer` (`dependency_types.rs`). The resolver reads it only through fallbacks, so every lookup the project's own data answers is unchanged: 32 33 - **Import map and named-type index:** a file the project's maps don't hold is looked up in the layer's (`ImportResolutionMap::fallback`, `NamedTypeIndex::fallback`). 34 - **Re-exports:** `follow_reexports` takes the loader's answer for a `(module, name)` it walked, instead of walking the package's stubs again; a module with no answer is walked as before. 35 - **Precedence (ADR 0014):** a declaration, the project's or a loaded dependency's, then a known shortcut, then a builtin. At the props-chain level a declaration that evaluates to nothing (cva's `VariantProps`, which needs `Parameters[0]`) gives way to a shortcut of the same name (`chain::known_fallback`), and its diagnostics are dropped with it. 36 37 - **Value index:** `ComponentProps` and `typeof X` in `extends` find a dependency component through `DependencyLayer::component`. Dependency components and enums live only in the layer's `GlobalSourceData`, so they never reach output or the bare-name indexes. 38 - **Const arrays:** `(typeof X)[number]` reads `X` as the symbol in scope in the file that wrote the type, project or dependency (`NamedTypeIndex::lookup_const_array`, with the dependency layer as the fallback), then the project's array of that name. An array is an `as const` literal or a `declare const X: readonly ["a", "b"]` annotation, which is how Radix declares `Align` and `Side`. 39 - **Diagnostics:** a type the loader could not find says why in the help of "Cannot resolve type" (`unresolved_type_help`): the module did not resolve, resolved to JavaScript without types, or does not export the name. 40 41 `chakra(element, { variants })` records the same literal variant keys as `cva(base, { variants })`. When `InferRecipeProps` refers to such a call, its shortcut preserves the recipe's `ConditionalValue` type, converts `"true"`/`"false"` keys to boolean, and leaves the alias unresolved when no variant config was recorded. 42 43 - **Collapse** (`collapse_inherited_props`, ADR 0012): `ctx.collapses` records an inherited source declaring more than 30 props as an `InheritedLayer` (no `html_element`, `total_props` = its declared count) and resolves only its notable members (`notable_html_attrs`' element-independent list) into `notable_inherited`. Interface-chain recordings are keyed on `expand_all` too. 44 45 **Invariant:** never merge layer data into the project's `GlobalSourceData`; that would emit dependency components and enums and let dependency names shadow project names in bare-name lookups. 46 47 ## Wrapper callees (`resolver/callee.rs`) 48 49 A component built by a generic call (`wrapperTypeArgument`, or `hocWrapper` with type arguments, as in `factory((props: P) => …)`) has the props its callee's result type declares; the props type its detection selected is the fallback when the callee or its result's props can't be evaluated. The extractor records every generic function's result in `SourceData::function_results`: the return annotation, or the type its only top-level `return … as T` asserts. `callee::result_chain` binds the callee's type parameters to the call's type arguments, follows aliases to the first React component type (`NamedExoticComponent

`, `FC

`, a call signature, …) and resolves P as the props chain (`Payload['props'] & RefAttributes<…> & { component?: any; … }`, through `evaluate.rs`). A name two members declare intersects, and `any` absorbs the intersection. For an undecidable conditional, the resolver keeps fields present in both branches, follows simple object aliases, and reports the partial result. If a factory type parameter still appears in `composes`, it fills missing props from the selected payload type; an explicit `any` from that type absorbs a tentative result type. The callee's file is a recorded dependency, so editing the factory re-resolves the components it builds; `follow_reexports` counts any declaration a file exports, so `export *` barrels reach it. The extractor's guesses among type arguments (a `props` payload member, a `*Props` name) now only decide detection: they reject 10 candidates across the five benchmark corpora. 50 51 Simple local aliases of generic factory functions share the original function result, and a function returning a local const initialized by a generic factory call follows that call's result. These paths cover Mantine's `Box` and `tableElement` wrappers. The generic type parameter in an undecidable conditional remains named and its unknown layers remain in `composes`.

Sources are an interface's own members and an object-literal alias; an interface's parents are sources of their own. Never at depth 0 (the component's own props type), and never while `ResolveState::expand_all` is set: `Pick`'s base and `keyof` operands select or count props by name. `Dependencies` (default) collapses loaded dependency files only; `All` adds every file outside `node_modules`, so React's and TypeScript's declarations stay with `html_attributes`. Interface-chain recordings are keyed on `expand_all` too. **Invariant:** never merge layer data into the project's `GlobalSourceData`; that would emit dependency components and enums and let dependency names shadow project names in bare-name lookups. ## Wrapper callees (`resolver/callee.rs`) A component built by a generic call (`wrapperTypeArgument`, or `hocWrapper` with type arguments, as in `factory((props: P) => …)`) has the props its callee's result type declares; the props type its detection selected is the fallback when the callee or its result's props can't be evaluated. The extractor records every generic function's result in `SourceData::function_results`: the return annotation, or the type its only top-level `return … as T` asserts. `callee::result_chain` binds the callee's type parameters to the call's type arguments, follows aliases to the first React component type (`NamedExoticComponent

`, `FC

`, a call signature, …) and resolves P as the props chain (`Payload['props'] & RefAttributes<…> & { component?: any; … }`, through `evaluate.rs`). A name two members declare intersects, and `any` absorbs the intersection. For an undecidable conditional, the resolver keeps fields present in both branches, follows simple object aliases, and reports the partial result. If a factory type parameter still appears in `composes`, it fills missing props from the selected payload type; an explicit `any` from that type absorbs a tentative result type. The callee's file is a recorded dependency, so editing the factory re-resolves the components it builds; `follow_reexports` counts any declaration a file exports, so `export *` barrels reach it. The extractor's guesses among type arguments (a `props` payload member, a `*Props` name) now only decide detection: they reject 10 candidates across the five benchmark corpora. Simple local aliases of generic factory functions share the original function result, and a function returning a local const initialized by a generic factory call follows that call's result. These paths cover Mantine's `Box` and `tableElement` wrappers. The generic type parameter in an undecidable conditional remains named and its unknown layers remain in `composes`.

1	# Status
2	
3	**Updated:** 2026-10-22
4	
5	Core extraction, resolver, CLI, NAPI binding, and Vite plugin all work and are fully tested. Config file loading, watch mode (including rebuilds on config changes and polling with `ensure_fresh`), plugin architecture, TOON token-optimized output format, JSON schema export, and bounded atomic DTS caching are implemented and verified.
6	
7	**Types from other packages.** Imports resolve to any file under a source directory, `.d.ts` included, so a monorepo whose packages are all source directories resolves across them. By default the declarations those names point to are loaded (ADR 0010, on by default since ADR 0019): a prop typed by an installed package resolves. `--no-load-dependencies` (config, NAPI and Vite `loadDependencies: false`) reads only `@types/react` and TypeScript's own lib files from `node_modules`, and then a prop whose type comes from any other installed package stays a named reference with an `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT` warning. Checked against RDT on five installed repos, loading reports far more of RDT's props and changes 11 matching types in 59,000. Chakra, the worst case, costs about 220 ms and 330 MiB against 50 ms and 100 MiB without (`docs/performance.md`).
8	
9	## Numbers
10	
11	- Rust tests (`cargo nextest` across the workspace, plus the NAPI binding tests) and vitest (unit with a mocked binding, integration against the real native binding), all green in CI
12	- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` clean with `unsafe_code = "deny"` enforced workspace-wide
13	- 20 real-world fixture libraries validated against `react-docgen-typescript` (shadcn, Radix, MUI, Chakra, Mantine, React Aria, antd, ariakit, ark-ui, base-ui, blueprint, day-picker, fluentui, headlessui, panda, react-final-form, react-resizable-panels, storybook-emotion, tanstack-table, zendesk-garden — see `rdt-coverage.md`)
14	- **Recall** against `react-docgen-typescript` with dependencies installed and loaded (`docs/measurement.md`, 2026-10-23): share of RDT's non-React props reported Mantine 99.7%, Chakra 98.6%, shadcn/ui 39.5%, Ant Design 80.3%, react-spectrum 99.7%.
15	- **Precision** per detection rule (`docs/precision.md`, 2026-10-21): 1 component that isn't one in 154 sampled, `functionDeclaration` 96% and every other rule 100%. 25 samples per rule can't yet establish the 95% gate.
16	- **Speed** on five pinned public corpora (`docs/performance.md`, 2026-10-22): 34 to 81 ms wall time and 66 to 153 MB peak RSS for 41 to 490 kLOC, 17 to 39 times faster than `react-docgen-typescript` on the same files. CI fails on a 10% regression against main or a ratio under 10×.
17	
18	## Features and improvements
19	
20	- **`htmlAttributes` defaults to `full`** (ADR 0024) — every attribute `@types/react` declares is listed, `ref` for `forwardRef` and `ComponentProps<"div">` props; `curated` is an opt-in compact mode. Costs against the old default: wall time +9 to +31%, peak RSS +12 to +37%, canonical JSON +42 to +105%.
21	- **Testing Stack** — `cargo-nextest` process runner, `rstest` parameterized spec tables, `insta` snapshots, and `trycmd` executable Markdown CLI specs.
22	- **Plugin system** (`DocgenPlugin` / `PluginRegistry`) — Extensible AST and component resolution hooks in `crates/core/src/plugin.rs`.
23	- **TOON output format** (`--format toon` / `toon.rs`) — Token-optimized format for LLM agents, cutting context window token usage by ~65-75%.
24	- **JSON schema export** (`caliper-docgen schema`) — Machine-readable Draft-07 JSON Schema export for component metadata validation.
25	- **Atomic & Bounded DTS cache** (`cache.rs`) — Atomic temp-file swap writes, dirty flag tracking, and 5,000 entry eviction cap.
26	- **Strict Safe Rust** — `unsafe_code = "deny"` via `[workspace.lints]`, active across all three crates (`core`, `cli`, `binding`) — none currently use `unsafe`, including the NAPI FFI boundary (napi-rs's `#[napi]` macros generate the glue without user-visible `unsafe`).
27	
28	## Known gaps that won't get fixed without a type checker
29	
30	See the "Known gaps summary" table in `rdt-coverage.md` for the full, maintained list. The short version: conditional types that need inference (`infer`, an unbound generic), mapped types over an unbound generic, and a couple of `@emotion/styled`-specific call shapes all need real type inference OXC deliberately doesn't do. Not bugs. A conditional, indexed access or mapped type whose operands are known is evaluated (`resolver/evaluate.rs`).
31	
32	An opt-in TypeScript 7 semantic backend is implemented as slice 1 (ADR 0006, ADR 0007), experimental and off by default: `extract --experimental-semantic-types`, see `type-checker-integration.md`. Accuracy is verified against real RDT — 0 missing/extra props on 13 hand-picked components, and re-verified on `7.1.0-beta` against the full 44-file fixture corpus (5,508/5,522 `required` matches, 5,266/5,522 type-string matches; the gap is explained noise, not a resolver bug) — and the RDT oracle that comparison depends on now runs on its own `typescript@6` install, separate from the semantic probe's `typescript@7.1.0-beta`. TypeScript 7.1's checker also runs, test-only, as an oracle for structural prop types (`docs/measurement.md`). A missing, crashed or timed-out `tsc` falls back to the structural result with one warning; the open lifecycle items are in `type-checker-integration.md`'s Gates table.
33	
34	## Experiments that didn't pan out
35	
36	**Confidence routing (2026-10-25).** The idea: score each component's risk of wrong or missing props from Caliper's own output, and ask the TypeScript 7.1 checker only about the risky ones. Measured against the checker on 518,268 shared props over the five corpora and the fixtures, routing 10% of components caught 23% of the props only the checker reports with the existing warning rule (a component with a degrade warning or error), against 3% for a smoothed table and 6% for a logistic model. At a 20% budget neither model caught the one prop the oracle marks `wrong`. Most of the checker-only props were Next's ambient augmentation (1,154 of 1,182 on shadcn) or false component matches, which a score of structural risk can't learn. So no score ships: warnings stay the signal, and on-demand checker use asks about the requested component instead of predicting. The script was deleted; the method is `scripts/parity.py oracle` plus the numbers above.
37	
38	## Where to look next
39	
40	- **Open gaps** → `edge-cases.md` — the gaps still open. Add one when you find a gap you aren't fixing now; delete it when you fix it.
41	- **What broke and why, historically** → `rdt-coverage.md` — every bug found during real-library validation, root cause, and the fix. Keep this updated; it's the project's memory.
42	- **Why a hard-to-reverse decision was made** → `docs/adr/` — OXC over the TypeScript compiler, manual serde for `PropType`, positional msgpack encoding, panic containment, the TypeScript 7 semantic backend. Write a new one when you make a decision like these (see `docs/adr/README.md`).
43	- **How the pipeline fits together** → `ARCHITECTURE.md`, and `docs/architecture/` for per-subsystem invariants and known gaps (moved from `.claude/semantic-model/` so every coding agent can read it, not just Claude Code — `AGENTS.md` is now this repo's shared instructions file, with per-tool mirrors under `.codex/`, `.cursor/`, `.gemini/`, `.github/`, `.opencode/`).
44	- **Setup, testing, code style, commit conventions** → `CONTRIBUTING.md`
45	- **Migrating from react-docgen-typescript** → `MIGRATING.md`

# Status

**Updated:** 2026-10-22

Core extraction, resolver, CLI, NAPI binding, and Vite plugin all work and are fully tested. Config file loading, watch mode (including rebuilds on config changes and polling with `ensure_fresh`), plugin architecture, TOON token-optimized output format, JSON schema export, and bounded atomic DTS caching are implemented and verified.

**Types from other packages.** Imports resolve to any file under a source directory, `.d.ts` included, so a monorepo whose packages are all source directories resolves across them. By default the declarations those names point to are loaded (ADR 0010, on by default since ADR 0019): a prop typed by an installed package resolves. `--no-load-dependencies` (config, NAPI and Vite `loadDependencies: false`) reads only `@types/react` and TypeScript's own lib files from `node_modules`, and then a prop whose type comes from any other installed package stays a named reference with an `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT` warning. Checked against RDT on five installed repos, loading reports far more of RDT's props and changes 11 matching types in 59,000. Chakra, the worst case, costs about 220 ms and 330 MiB against 50 ms and 100 MiB without (`docs/performance.md`).

## Numbers

- Rust tests (`cargo nextest` across the workspace, plus the NAPI binding tests) and vitest (unit with a mocked binding, integration against the real native binding), all green in CI
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` clean with `unsafe_code = "deny"` enforced workspace-wide
- 20 real-world fixture libraries validated against `react-docgen-typescript` (shadcn, Radix, MUI, Chakra, Mantine, React Aria, antd, ariakit, ark-ui, base-ui, blueprint, day-picker, fluentui, headlessui, panda, react-final-form, react-resizable-panels, storybook-emotion, tanstack-table, zendesk-garden — see `rdt-coverage.md`)
- **Recall** against `react-docgen-typescript` with dependencies installed and loaded (`docs/measurement.md`, 2026-10-23): share of RDT's non-React props reported Mantine 99.7%, Chakra 98.6%, shadcn/ui 39.5%, Ant Design 80.3%, react-spectrum 99.7%.
- **Precision** per detection rule (`docs/precision.md`, 2026-10-21): 1 component that isn't one in 154 sampled, `functionDeclaration` 96% and every other rule 100%. 25 samples per rule can't yet establish the 95% gate.
- **Speed** on five pinned public corpora (`docs/performance.md`, 2026-10-22): 34 to 81 ms wall time and 66 to 153 MB peak RSS for 41 to 490 kLOC, 17 to 39 times faster than `react-docgen-typescript` on the same files. CI fails on a 10% regression against main or a ratio under 10×.

## Features and improvements

- **`htmlAttributes` defaults to `full`** (ADR 0024) — every attribute `@types/react` declares is listed, `ref` for `forwardRef` and `ComponentProps<"div">` props; `curated` is an opt-in compact mode. Costs against the old default: wall time +9 to +31%, peak RSS +12 to +37%, canonical JSON +42 to +105%.
- **Testing Stack** — `cargo-nextest` process runner, `rstest` parameterized spec tables, `insta` snapshots, and `trycmd` executable Markdown CLI specs.
- **Plugin system** (`DocgenPlugin` / `PluginRegistry`) — Extensible AST and component resolution hooks in `crates/core/src/plugin.rs`.
- **TOON output format** (`--format toon` / `toon.rs`) — Token-optimized format for LLM agents, cutting context window token usage by ~65-75%.
- **JSON schema export** (`caliper-docgen schema`) — Machine-readable Draft-07 JSON Schema export for component metadata validation.
- **Atomic & Bounded DTS cache** (`cache.rs`) — Atomic temp-file swap writes, dirty flag tracking, and 5,000 entry eviction cap.
- **Strict Safe Rust** — `unsafe_code = "deny"` via `[workspace.lints]`, active across all three crates (`core`, `cli`, `binding`) — none currently use `unsafe`, including the NAPI FFI boundary (napi-rs's `#[napi]` macros generate the glue without user-visible `unsafe`).

## Known gaps that won't get fixed without a type checker

See the "Known gaps summary" table in `rdt-coverage.md` for the full, maintained list. The short version: conditional types that need inference (`infer`, an unbound generic), mapped types over an unbound generic, and a couple of `@emotion/styled`-specific call shapes all need real type inference OXC deliberately doesn't do. Not bugs. A conditional, indexed access or mapped type whose operands are known is evaluated (`resolver/evaluate.rs`).

An opt-in TypeScript 7 semantic backend is implemented as slice 1 (ADR 0006, ADR 0007), experimental and off by default: `extract --experimental-semantic-types`, see `type-checker-integration.md`. Accuracy is verified against real RDT — 0 missing/extra props on 13 hand-picked components, and re-verified on `7.1.0-beta` against the full 44-file fixture corpus (5,508/5,522 `required` matches, 5,266/5,522 type-string matches; the gap is explained noise, not a resolver bug) — and the RDT oracle that comparison depends on now runs on its own `typescript@6` install, separate from the semantic probe's `typescript@7.1.0-beta`. TypeScript 7.1's checker also runs, test-only, as an oracle for structural prop types (`docs/measurement.md`). A missing, crashed or timed-out `tsc` falls back to the structural result with one warning; the open lifecycle items are in `type-checker-integration.md`'s Gates table.

## Experiments that didn't pan out

**Confidence routing (2026-10-25).** The idea: score each component's risk of wrong or missing props from Caliper's own output, and ask the TypeScript 7.1 checker only about the risky ones. Measured against the checker on 518,268 shared props over the five corpora and the fixtures, routing 10% of components caught 23% of the props only the checker reports with the existing warning rule (a component with a degrade warning or error), against 3% for a smoothed table and 6% for a logistic model. At a 20% budget neither model caught the one prop the oracle marks `wrong`. Most of the checker-only props were Next's ambient augmentation (1,154 of 1,182 on shadcn) or false component matches, which a score of structural risk can't learn. So no score ships: warnings stay the signal, and on-demand checker use asks about the requested component instead of predicting. The script was deleted; the method is `scripts/parity.py oracle` plus the numbers above.

## Where to look next

- **Open gaps** → `edge-cases.md` — the gaps still open. Add one when you find a gap you aren't fixing now; delete it when you fix it.
- **What broke and why, historically** → `rdt-coverage.md` — every bug found during real-library validation, root cause, and the fix. Keep this updated; it's the project's memory.
- **Why a hard-to-reverse decision was made** → `docs/adr/` — OXC over the TypeScript compiler, manual serde for `PropType`, positional msgpack encoding, panic containment, the TypeScript 7 semantic backend. Write a new one when you make a decision like these (see `docs/adr/README.md`).
- **How the pipeline fits together** → `ARCHITECTURE.md`, and `docs/architecture/` for per-subsystem invariants and known gaps (moved from `.claude/semantic-model/` so every coding agent can read it, not just Claude Code — `AGENTS.md` is now this repo's shared instructions file, with per-tool mirrors under `.codex/`, `.cursor/`, `.gemini/`, `.github/`, `.opencode/`).
- **Setup, testing, code style, commit conventions** → `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- **Migrating from react-docgen-typescript** → `MIGRATING.md`

## Code style

The authoritative reference is `.claude/skills/rust-style/SKILL.md`. Highlights:

**Maps:** `FxHashMap` for internal maps (hot path, no DoS surface). `BTreeMap` for anything that ends up in JSON output (key ordering must be deterministic and stable across runs).

**Strings:** `CompactString` for type names and prop names. Most are ≤24 bytes (`string`, `boolean`, `ReactNode`, `MouseEvent`) and fit inline without heap allocation.

**Control flow:** `let...else` keeps the happy path flat:

```rust
let Some(entry) = map.get(key) else { return None };
```

**Matching on project-local enums:** no wildcards. `match status { Ok => .., Err => .. }` gives a compile error when new variants are added. `match status { Ok => .., _ => .. }` silently ignores them.

**No `unwrap()` outside tests.** Use `?` or emit a `Diagnostic` and return a safe default. The `Diagnostic` type has constructors for common error shapes.

**Comments:** only when the WHY is non-obvious. Not what the code does.

- `feat:` / `fix:` / `refactor:` / `chore:` / `docs:` prefix


1. Branch from `main`

1	# NAPI binding
2	
3	**Source:** `crates/binding/src/lib.rs`, `crates/binding/build.rs`
4	
5	This is the only consumer-facing FFI boundary in the workspace: a thin `cdylib` that Node.js (concretely, a Vite plugin) calls into. It owns no extraction logic — every entry point marshals `JsExtractOptions` into `PipelineOptions` and delegates straight to `caliper_docgen_core::pipeline`. Its entire job is getting values across the Rust/JS boundary without ever letting a Rust panic reach the Node process, and without ever handing a caller anything other than a proper JS `Error` on failure.
6	
7	## NAPI entry points
8	
9	- `extract_all(options) -> String` — cold, one-shot extraction. Runs inside `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`.
10	- `create_session(options) -> u32` — allocates a session ID, builds a `WatchSession`, inserts it into `SESSIONS`. Runs **synchronously on the calling (JS) thread** — no `spawn_blocking`.
11	- `initialize_session(session_id, options) -> String` — looks up or lazily creates the session, then returns `WatchSession::initialize()`: the session's current output, running the cold extraction first if the session has none. The Vite plugin's virtual-module `load` uses it as the snapshot. Runs inside `spawn_blocking`.
12	- `extract_file_incremental(file_path, session_id, options) -> String` — looks up or lazily creates the session, then runs `WatchSession::update_file()`. Runs inside `spawn_blocking`.
13	- `session_docgen_info(session_id, keys) -> String` — the named components of the session's current revision in react-docgen-typescript's `__docgenInfo` shape (`pipeline::rdt::docgen_info`), for the Storybook provider (`packages/storybook`). Reads `WatchSession::current_output` without copying it; a key the session lacks, or any key before `initialize_session`, is left out. On a lazy session (below) it resolves the requested components now and answers the rest from the session's memo. Runs synchronously on the calling thread, with `contain_panic` directly.
14	- `session_component_keys(session_id) -> Vec<String>` and `session_stats(session_id) -> Option<JsLazyStats>` — the keys `session_docgen_info` answers, and what a lazy session has indexed and resolved (`components`, `resolved`, `dependencyFiles`). Synchronous; empty or `None` for an unknown or uninitialized session, and `session_stats` is `None` for an eager one.
15	- `ensure_fresh(session_id) -> String` — runs `WatchSession::ensure_fresh()`: stats every file the session read and applies what changed since, for a host without a file watcher. Errors for an unknown session, since it has no options to create one from. Runs inside `spawn_blocking`.
16	- `resolution_config_files(session_id) -> Vec<String>` and `is_resolution_config(session_id, file_path) -> bool` — the configs a watcher adds, and whether a changed path is one. Synchronous; empty or false for an unknown session.
17	- `close_session(session_id) -> ()` — removes the session from `SESSIONS`. Runs synchronously on the calling thread, like `create_session`.
18	
19	**Lazy sessions (ADR 0016).** `JsExtractOptions.lazy: true` on `create_session` (or on the auto-vivifying `initialize_session` and `extract_file_incremental`) makes a `WatchSession::lazy`. `initialize_session` then parses and indexes every file and returns an `ExtractionOutput` with no components; `extract_file_incremental` and `ensure_fresh` return an `IncrementalUpdate` with `updatedKeys` and `removedKeys` for the memoized components the change can affect, and no `updatedComponents`. Without `lazy` every entry point behaves as before.
20	
21	`SESSIONS` is `static SESSIONS: LazyLock<DashMap<u32, Arc<WatchSession>>>` — a single process-wide session table. `initialize_session` and `extract_file_incremental` both tolerate a missing session ID by silently constructing a fresh `WatchSession` from the passed `options` and inserting it (`lib.rs:171-179`, `200-208`) — this is a lazy-recovery path, not an error case, so a caller that races `create_session` against `initialize_session` (or never calls `create_session` at all) still gets a working session rather than an "unknown session ID" error.
22	
23	## Panic-containment boundary (LOCKED DESIGN DECISION — ADR 0005)
24	
25	Every entry point wraps its real body in `caliper_docgen_core::panic_guard::contain_panic(label, closure)`. This is not incidental defense — it is a deliberate, documented design decision (`docs/adr/0005-panic-containment-boundary.md`) with a specific and non-obvious shape:
26	
27	- **The `spawn_blocking`-wrapped entry points** (`extract_all`, `initialize_session`, `extract_file_incremental`, `ensure_fresh`) put `contain_panic` **inside** the `spawn_blocking` closure, not around it. Before ADR 0005, these three were only accidentally panic-safe: `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`'s `JoinError` happens to catch an unwind as a side effect of tokio's own plumbing, not because anyone decided panic-safety belonged there. Wrapping in `contain_panic` too makes the guarantee a designed one, converts the panic into a `Diagnostic`-derived `napi::Error` message instead of an opaque `JoinError`, and stops being contingent on tokio's internals never changing.
28	- **`create_session` and `close_session` get `contain_panic` directly**, with no `spawn_blocking` at all, because they run synchronously on the thread the JS call arrived on. Before ADR 0005 these two had **zero** panic protection — not even the accidental kind — whether a panic there crashed the Node process depended on whether napi-rs's codegen auto-wraps in `catch_unwind`, which was never verified. ADR 0005 closes that gap directly rather than relying on napi-rs's opt-in `#[napi(catch_unwind)]` attribute (considered and rejected in the ADR's "Alternatives considered" section, in favor of one mechanism — `contain_panic` — shared across rayon, plugin hooks, and FFI instead of two different ones). Do not remove or "simplify away" the `contain_panic` wrapping in `create_session`/`close_session` on the theory that synchronous code "can't really panic" — `next_session_id()`, `WatchSession::new()`, and `PipelineOptions::try_from` all run inside that closure, and `WatchSession::new` is not a leaf function under this crate's own non-negotiables (no `unwrap()` outside `#[cfg(test)]`, but a _panic_ — e.g. an indexing panic or arithmetic overflow in debug builds — is a different failure mode than `unwrap()` and is exactly what `contain_panic` exists to catch regardless of whether the non-negotiables are honored everywhere upstream).
29	
30	## Why this crate's panic discipline is higher-stakes than `crates/cli`'s
31	
32	`panic_guard::contain_panic` is shared code — the same function backs rayon `.map()` closures in `pipeline/mod.rs`, `DocgenPlugin` hook calls in `plugin.rs`, and all six entry points here. But the failure mode on the other side of an _uncaught_ panic differs by boundary. `crates/cli` is a standalone binary process: an uncaught panic there kills one CLI invocation, and the OS process boundary means nothing else is affected. This crate is a `cdylib` loaded **in-process** into a long-running Node.js server (a Vite dev server, per the doc comments on `create_session`/`initialize_session`/`close_session` referencing `configResolved`/`configureServer`/`buildEnd`). An uncaught Rust panic crossing the FFI boundary here does not fail one call — it is undefined behavior at best and a hard crash of the entire Node process at worst, taking down every other request the dev server was serving. That asymmetry is why `contain_panic` at this boundary is load-bearing in a way it is only "good hygiene" for `crates/cli`: bypass it here and the blast radius is the whole host process, not one invocation.
33	
34	## Error conversion: everything converges on `napi::Error::from_reason(String)`
35	
36	Every fallible path in this file — `PipelineOptions::try_from` validation failures, `contain_panic`'s caught-panic `Diagnostic`, `extraction_output_to_json`/`incremental_update_to_json` serialization errors, and `spawn_blocking`'s own `JoinError` — is mapped through `.map_err(|e| napi::Error::from_reason(e.to_string()))` or the equivalent `Err(diag) => Err(napi::Error::from_reason(diag.to_string()))` arm. There is no code path in this file that lets a `Result::Err` propagate to napi-rs's codegen in any form other than `napi::Error`.
37

# NAPI binding

**Source:** `crates/binding/src/lib.rs`, `crates/binding/build.rs`

This is the only consumer-facing FFI boundary in the workspace: a thin `cdylib` that Node.js (concretely, a Vite plugin) calls into. It owns no extraction logic — every entry point marshals `JsExtractOptions` into `PipelineOptions` and delegates straight to `caliper_docgen_core::pipeline`. Its entire job is getting values across the Rust/JS boundary without ever letting a Rust panic reach the Node process, and without ever handing a caller anything other than a proper JS `Error` on failure.

## NAPI entry points

- `extract_all(options) -> String` — cold, one-shot extraction. Runs inside `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`.
- `create_session(options) -> u32` — allocates a session ID, builds a `WatchSession`, inserts it into `SESSIONS`. Runs **synchronously on the calling (JS) thread** — no `spawn_blocking`.
- `initialize_session(session_id, options) -> String` — looks up or lazily creates the session, then returns `WatchSession::initialize()`: the session's current output, running the cold extraction first if the session has none. The Vite plugin's virtual-module `load` uses it as the snapshot. Runs inside `spawn_blocking`.
- `extract_file_incremental(file_path, session_id, options) -> String` — looks up or lazily creates the session, then runs `WatchSession::update_file()`. Runs inside `spawn_blocking`.
- `session_docgen_info(session_id, keys) -> String` — the named components of the session's current revision in react-docgen-typescript's `__docgenInfo` shape (`pipeline::rdt::docgen_info`), for the Storybook provider (`packages/storybook`). Reads `WatchSession::current_output` without copying it; a key the session lacks, or any key before `initialize_session`, is left out. On a lazy session (below) it resolves the requested components now and answers the rest from the session's memo. Runs synchronously on the calling thread, with `contain_panic` directly.
- `session_component_keys(session_id) -> Vec<String>` and `session_stats(session_id) -> Option<JsLazyStats>` — the keys `session_docgen_info` answers, and what a lazy session has indexed and resolved (`components`, `resolved`, `dependencyFiles`). Synchronous; empty or `None` for an unknown or uninitialized session, and `session_stats` is `None` for an eager one.
- `ensure_fresh(session_id) -> String` — runs `WatchSession::ensure_fresh()`: stats every file the session read and applies what changed since, for a host without a file watcher. Errors for an unknown session, since it has no options to create one from. Runs inside `spawn_blocking`.
- `resolution_config_files(session_id) -> Vec<String>` and `is_resolution_config(session_id, file_path) -> bool` — the configs a watcher adds, and whether a changed path is one. Synchronous; empty or false for an unknown session.
- `close_session(session_id) -> ()` — removes the session from `SESSIONS`. Runs synchronously on the calling thread, like `create_session`.

**Lazy sessions (ADR 0016).** `JsExtractOptions.lazy: true` on `create_session` (or on the auto-vivifying `initialize_session` and `extract_file_incremental`) makes a `WatchSession::lazy`. `initialize_session` then parses and indexes every file and returns an `ExtractionOutput` with no components; `extract_file_incremental` and `ensure_fresh` return an `IncrementalUpdate` with `updatedKeys` and `removedKeys` for the memoized components the change can affect, and no `updatedComponents`. Without `lazy` every entry point behaves as before.

`SESSIONS` is `static SESSIONS: LazyLock<DashMap<u32, Arc<WatchSession>>>` — a single process-wide session table. `initialize_session` and `extract_file_incremental` both tolerate a missing session ID by silently constructing a fresh `WatchSession` from the passed `options` and inserting it (`lib.rs:171-179`, `200-208`) — this is a lazy-recovery path, not an error case, so a caller that races `create_session` against `initialize_session` (or never calls `create_session` at all) still gets a working session rather than an "unknown session ID" error.

## Panic-containment boundary (LOCKED DESIGN DECISION — ADR 0005)

Every entry point wraps its real body in `caliper_docgen_core::panic_guard::contain_panic(label, closure)`. This is not incidental defense — it is a deliberate, documented design decision (`docs/adr/0005-panic-containment-boundary.md`) with a specific and non-obvious shape:

- **The `spawn_blocking`-wrapped entry points** (`extract_all`, `initialize_session`, `extract_file_incremental`, `ensure_fresh`) put `contain_panic` **inside** the `spawn_blocking` closure, not around it. Before ADR 0005, these three were only accidentally panic-safe: `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`'s `JoinError` happens to catch an unwind as a side effect of tokio's own plumbing, not because anyone decided panic-safety belonged there. Wrapping in `contain_panic` too makes the guarantee a designed one, converts the panic into a `Diagnostic`-derived `napi::Error` message instead of an opaque `JoinError`, and stops being contingent on tokio's internals never changing.
- **`create_session` and `close_session` get `contain_panic` directly**, with no `spawn_blocking` at all, because they run synchronously on the thread the JS call arrived on. Before ADR 0005 these two had **zero** panic protection — not even the accidental kind — whether a panic there crashed the Node process depended on whether napi-rs's codegen auto-wraps in `catch_unwind`, which was never verified. ADR 0005 closes that gap directly rather than relying on napi-rs's opt-in `#[napi(catch_unwind)]` attribute (considered and rejected in the ADR's "Alternatives considered" section, in favor of one mechanism — `contain_panic` — shared across rayon, plugin hooks, and FFI instead of two different ones). Do not remove or "simplify away" the `contain_panic` wrapping in `create_session`/`close_session` on the theory that synchronous code "can't really panic" — `next_session_id()`, `WatchSession::new()`, and `PipelineOptions::try_from` all run inside that closure, and `WatchSession::new` is not a leaf function under this crate's own non-negotiables (no `unwrap()` outside `#[cfg(test)]`, but a _panic_ — e.g. an indexing panic or arithmetic overflow in debug builds — is a different failure mode than `unwrap()` and is exactly what `contain_panic` exists to catch regardless of whether the non-negotiables are honored everywhere upstream).

## Why this crate's panic discipline is higher-stakes than `crates/cli`'s

`panic_guard::contain_panic` is shared code — the same function backs rayon `.map()` closures in `pipeline/mod.rs`, `DocgenPlugin` hook calls in `plugin.rs`, and all six entry points here. But the failure mode on the other side of an _uncaught_ panic differs by boundary. `crates/cli` is a standalone binary process: an uncaught panic there kills one CLI invocation, and the OS process boundary means nothing else is affected. This crate is a `cdylib` loaded **in-process** into a long-running Node.js server (a Vite dev server, per the doc comments on `create_session`/`initialize_session`/`close_session` referencing `configResolved`/`configureServer`/`buildEnd`). An uncaught Rust panic crossing the FFI boundary here does not fail one call — it is undefined behavior at best and a hard crash of the entire Node process at worst, taking down every other request the dev server was serving. That asymmetry is why `contain_panic` at this boundary is load-bearing in a way it is only "good hygiene" for `crates/cli`: bypass it here and the blast radius is the whole host process, not one invocation.

## Error conversion: everything converges on `napi::Error::from_reason(String)`

Every fallible path in this file — `PipelineOptions::try_from` validation failures, `contain_panic`'s caught-panic `Diagnostic`, `extraction_output_to_json`/`incremental_update_to_json` serialization errors, and `spawn_blocking`'s own `JoinError` — is mapped through `.map_err(|e| napi::Error::from_reason(e.to_string()))` or the equivalent `Err(diag) => Err(napi::Error::from_reason(diag.to_string()))` arm. There is no code path in this file that lets a `Result::Err` propagate to napi-rs's codegen in any form other than `napi::Error`.

**Invariant 1: no Node caller of any of the six entry points can ever receive anything other than a resolved value or a proper JS `Error` — never an opaque crash, never a native panic message, never a bare Rust `Result` leaking through.** This is what makes `extract_all`/`initialize_session`/`extract_file_incremental`'s doubled `Result` handling (`spawn_blocking`'s `JoinError` outside, `contain_panic`'s `Result<T, Diagnostic>` inside) necessary rather than redundant — two independent failure channels (task-join failure, application-level panic) both have to be funneled into the one JS-visible error type.

**Invariant 2: `htmlAttributes` never silently defaults.** `TryFrom<JsExtractOptions> for PipelineOptions` treats every `Option<T>` field as "use `PipelineOptions::default()`" when `None`, _except_ `html_attributes`, which goes through `HtmlAttributeMode::parse` and hard-errors, naming the bad value, if the caller (e.g. via a TypeScript `as any` cast bypassing the `'curated' | 'full' | 'none'` `ts_type`) passes something that isn't one of the three accepted strings. This is a deliberate application of AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 ("never fail silently") at the boundary where TypeScript's type system stops being a real guarantee.

**Invariant 3: `extraPathsJson`/`knownTypeOverridesJson` malformed JSON is a hard `Err`, never a silently-empty map.** Both fields are accepted as raw JSON strings specifically "to avoid napi object complexity" (`lib.rs:50`) — `serde_json::from_str` failure is mapped to an error naming the field (`"extraPaths is not valid JSON: {e}"` / `"knownTypeOverrides is not valid JSON: {e}"`), not swallowed into `Default::default()`. Covered directly by `malformed_extra_paths_json_is_a_hard_error_not_a_silent_empty_map` and its `known_type_overrides` sibling in the test module.
