# 0019. Load dependency declarations by default

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-25 **Supersedes:** the "off by default" clause of [0010](0010-load-dependency-declarations-by-name.md)

## Context

ADR 0010 shipped dependency loading off by default because of its cost: Chakra took 497 ms and 1.3 GB with it on, against 43 ms and 82 MiB without (`docs/performance.md`, 2026-10-23). `docs/STATUS.md` named that cost as the blocker. The Storybook addon already defaults `loadDependencies` to `true` (#155), so the CLI, the config file, the Vite plugin and the NAPI binding were the only surfaces where a prop typed by an installed package stayed a named reference with an `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT` warning.

The cost moved. Memo replay, `keyof` name walks, interned keys and a parallel lib parse (#136, #175, #177, #178, #182) took Chakra to about 220 ms and 330 MiB.

## Decision

`PipelineOptions::load_dependencies` defaults to `true`. `--no-load-dependencies` (CLI), `loadDependencies: false` (`docgen.config.ts`, NAPI `JsExtractOptions`, Vite plugin, Storybook addon) turn it off, and a flag overrides the config. `--load-dependencies` stays accepted and means the same as the default, so existing scripts keep working; it conflicts with `--no-load-dependencies`.

A project with no packages installed loads nothing, so there is nothing to opt out of there.

## Consequences

Measured on the five parity corpora, `extract --json`, best of 7, interleaved, on a laptop shared with other jobs (about ±10 ms), old default against new default:

| Corpus   |  Wall ms | Peak RSS MiB |           Props | Unresolved warnings |
| -------- | -------: | -----------: | --------------: | ------------------: |
| mantine  |  50 → 60 |    112 → 128 | 19,834 → 19,834 |             14 → 10 |
| chakra   | 50 → 220 |    101 → 330 |   592 → 479,235 |             315 → 0 |
| shadcn   |  50 → 90 |    101 → 225 |   1,543 → 8,131 |           816 → 190 |
| antd     |  40 → 50 |     95 → 114 |   3,349 → 3,856 |              76 → 8 |
| spectrum |  70 → 90 |    136 → 161 | 32,585 → 32,587 |              13 → 5 |

- **Output is exact.** On all five corpora the new default is byte-identical to the previous build's `--load-dependencies` output, and `--no-load-dependencies` is byte-identical to the previous default (canonical JSON without `durationMs` and `stats`).
- **Accuracy against react-docgen-typescript.** Share of its props reported, off → on (the 0.4.0 parity baseline, since removed; not re-measured here): Chakra 0.1% → 98.6%, shadcn 6.4% → 39.5%, antd 71.8% → 80.3%, Mantine and Spectrum 99.7% both.
- **The cost lands on a few projects.** Chakra is 4.4× slower and holds 3.3× the memory by default; shadcn takes 40 ms and 124 MiB more. Mantine, antd and Spectrum take 10 to 20 ms and 16 to 25 MiB more. A CI job that needs the old speed passes `--no-load-dependencies`.
- **No packages installed.** antd's `components` copied without `node_modules`: 3,349 props and 163 unresolved warnings either way, 40 ms with loading on against 30 ms off. One diagnostic's help text differs, because it says dependency types were loaded but a module could not be found.
- **Tools that pinned the old default** (the parity script, `apps/validate/src/run-ours.ts`, the corpus snapshot tests) now pin it explicitly, so their baselines keep their meaning.
- **A changed default, not a changed API.** `PipelineOptions` keeps its shape; the changeset is a minor bump.

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep it off and rely on the addon.** The CLI and plugin would keep reporting hundreds of unresolved names on installed projects (816 on shadcn) while the addon did not.
- **Turn it on only when a `node_modules` directory is found.** That is what loading already does: with no packages, the layer is empty. A second switch would add a mode with the same effect.
- **Flip the plugin and addon only.** It leaves the CLI and the config file disagreeing with the tools built on them.

# 0023. Function parameters carry `optional` and `rest`, and the canonical JSON moves to version 3

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-26

## Context

A function type lost two things about its parameters. OXC keeps `...rest` apart from the other parameters, and the extractor read only the others, so `(...args: any[]) => void` printed as `() => void`. It also dropped the `?`, so `(a?: string) => void` printed as `(a: string) => void`. A caller reading the signature, Storybook or an agent, then believes an argument is required or that none are accepted. The type-loss measurement on current `main` (PR #230) counted rest parameters lost on Mantine 380, antd 140 (102 distinct props), Chakra 15,182 (repeats of the same style props), shadcn 12 and Spectrum 12.

## Decision

A parameter is required, optional (`a?: T`) or the rest parameter (`...a: T[]`). The extractor records the kind per parameter next to its name (`CollectedType::Function::param_kinds`, cache schema 25), and the rest parameter is appended last with its array type as written. `FunctionParam` gains `optional` and `rest`, written to the canonical JSON only when true. `raw_string` prints `a?: T` and `...a: T[]`, which is what the RDT format shows. TOON prints `T?` and `...T`. `structural_hash` includes both flags, so two signatures that differ only by a flag are not interned together.

`SCHEMA_VERSION` moves from 2 to 3. ADR 0017 says not to bump for an addition a reader can ignore. This one is not ignorable: a version 2 reader would show `...args: any[]` as a required parameter named `args`, a wrong signature, and would never have seen a rest parameter before. The Vite plugin and the Storybook addon read version 3 only.

## Not done here

- **`readonly`:** the extractor peels `readonly` from `readonly string[]` on purpose (`extractor/mod.rs`), and the loss table counts it on 540 distinct Chakra types, 101 shadcn, 26 antd and 33 Spectrum. Carrying it needs a flag on `PropType::Array` and `Tuple` and on their collected forms, in the union normalizer, the evaluator's assignability and every printer. A control for an array is the same either way, so the gain is signature fidelity only.
- **`RefObject` shown as `Ref`:** `resolver/react.rs` maps `Ref`, `RefObject`, `ForwardedRef`, `MutableRefObject`, `RefCallback` and `LegacyRef` to one `PropType::Ref { element }`. Telling them apart needs a kind on that variant. Sixteen distinct shadcn types print `Ref<T>` for `RefObject<T>`.

Either would be another schema bump, so they should land together.

## Consequences

- Every installed reader moves with the writer. A mismatch fails at the first read with the message from ADR 0017.
- An old parse cache is discarded once (schema 24 to 25).
- The semantic backend (TS 7.1) does not set the new fields yet: `crates/semantic/src/convert.rs` builds each parameter from its name and type, so its signatures come out with every parameter required.
- Output grows by a handful of bytes per optional or rest parameter, and by the rest parameters that were missing entirely.

# 0024. List every HTML attribute React declares by default

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-26 **Supersedes:** the "curated by default" clause of [0013](0013-curated-mode-reads-react-attributes-apart.md) and the `htmlAttributes` default recorded in `docs/rdt-coverage.md`

## Context

`htmlAttributes: 'curated'` was the default. It was meant to keep the props table short, but it left props React declares out of the answer: `--format rdt` and the addon's `docgenInfo` never emitted `notableInherited` at all, so no handler of a curated component reached Storybook. A props type that reached an element through `Omit<HTMLAttributes<…>>`, `ComponentProps<"div">` or `PropsWithoutRef<…>` had no element layer in `full` either (antd's `PurePanel`, `Dragger`'s `capture`, `ref` on `forwardRef` components).

The Storybook addon's `collapseInheritedProps` already hides props inherited from dependencies, so a long list in the output does not make the UI long.

## Decision

`PipelineOptions::html_attributes` defaults to `full`: the CLI, `docgen.config.ts`, the NAPI binding, the Vite plugin and the Storybook addon all follow, and `skipHtmlProps` still means `none`. `curated` stays as an opt-in compact mode: `ref`, `aria-*`, every event handler but the `*Capture` twins, the global attributes and the element's notable ones, read from React's declarations and listed beside `props` in `--format rdt`. `key` is omitted in every mode; `ref` is listed for `ComponentProps<"div">` props and for `forwardRef` components.

Without `@types/react`, `full` lists no inherited attributes and reports one info diagnostic per component that needed them.

## Consequences

Measured on the five parity corpora with dependencies loaded (the default), canonical JSON, no cache, median of 11 (wall) and 21 (CPU, peak RSS), old default (`curated` at 338d1ddc) → new default:

| Corpus   |   Wall ms |       CPU s | Peak RSS MiB |     JSON MB |
| -------- | --------: | ----------: | -----------: | ----------: |
| antd     |   56 → 62 | 0.33 → 0.37 |    130 → 151 |   3.6 → 6.3 |

# 0024. List every HTML attribute React declares by default

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-26 **Supersedes:** the "curated by default" clause of [0013](0013-curated-mode-reads-react-attributes-apart.md) and the `htmlAttributes` default recorded in `docs/rdt-coverage.md`

## Context

`htmlAttributes: 'curated'` was the default. It was meant to keep the props table short, but it left props React declares out of the answer: `--format rdt` and the addon's `docgenInfo` never emitted `notableInherited` at all, so no handler of a curated component reached Storybook. A props type that reached an element through `Omit<HTMLAttributes<…>>`, `ComponentProps<"div">` or `PropsWithoutRef<…>` had no element layer in `full` either (antd's `PurePanel`, `Dragger`'s `capture`, `ref` on `forwardRef` components).

The Storybook addon's `collapseInheritedProps` already hides props inherited from dependencies, so a long list in the output does not make the UI long.

## Decision

`PipelineOptions::html_attributes` defaults to `full`: the CLI, `docgen.config.ts`, the NAPI binding, the Vite plugin and the Storybook addon all follow, and `skipHtmlProps` still means `none`. `curated` stays as an opt-in compact mode: `ref`, `aria-*`, every event handler but the `*Capture` twins, the global attributes and the element's notable ones, read from React's declarations and listed beside `props` in `--format rdt`. `key` is omitted in every mode; `ref` is listed for `ComponentProps<"div">` props and for `forwardRef` components.

# 0021. Publish the semantic backend crates with the CLI

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-25

## Context

The 0.6.0 release published `caliper-docgen-core`, then Cargo rejected `caliper-docgen` because its `caliper-docgen-semantic` dependency had only a local path. Both the semantic backend and its `caliper-docgen-tsc-client` dependency were marked `publish = false`. ADR 0007 requires the backend in every CLI build, with activation controlled at runtime, so the published CLI also needs both crates from crates.io.

## Decision

Publish `caliper-docgen-tsc-client` and `caliper-docgen-semantic` as separate crates. Every path dependency in their chain and in `caliper-docgen` has a version requirement. Callisto includes the two crates as crates.io release packages so it can publish them before the CLI. The backend remains off at runtime unless requested.

## Consequences

- Cargo can package the CLI from registry dependencies, and Callisto can order the transport, backend and CLI publications by dependency.
- The two backend crates become public distributions whose versions and API compatibility need release maintenance.
- The failed 0.6.0 release commit cannot be repaired by rerunning its immutable source; a new release must include these manifest changes.

## Alternatives considered

- Move the backend and transport code into the CLI crate. That removes the registry dependencies but collapses two existing crate boundaries and makes the CLI own the process transport.
- Exclude the backend from the published CLI. That would make the binary depend on how it was built, reversing ADR 0007's always-compiled contract.

## HtmlAttributeMode: curated / full / none

`PipelineOptions.html_attributes` (CLI: `--html-attributes <curated|full|none>`; NAPI: `htmlAttributes: 'curated' | 'full' | 'none'`; config file: `htmlAttributes` in `docgen.config.ts`) controls how much of an inherited HTML element's attribute surface gets exposed:

- **Curated** — opt-in compact mode: a subset per element (`ref`, `aria-*`, every handler but the `*Capture` twins, the global attributes, the element's notable ones) in `notableInherited`, which `--format rdt` and `docgenInfo` list beside `props`.
- **Full (default)** — actually resolves `@types/react`'s real `HTMLAttributes`/`AriaAttributes`/`DOMAttributes`/`<Element>HTMLAttributes` interface chain (merged into `GlobalSourceData` by the pipeline, looked up by the resolver like any other interface) and merges the real fields directly into `props` — matching how RDT flattens everything into one props map. Verified against a real button: 238 of ~250 real attributes resolve (the remainder is a narrower, separate gap — see below). Costs ~16ms once per `@types/react` version (cached the same way any other `.d.ts` is), not per extraction run.
- **None** — no inherited HTML attributes synthesized at all; own props only.

**Known residual gap, not fixed:** a handful of fields inside `@types/react`'s own interface chain (`AriaAttributes` referenced bare from within the same enclosing `declare namespace React {}` block, not through an explicit `React.` qualifier) don't resolve — same-namespace _sibling_ reference resolution is narrower than the namespace-_qualified_ reference resolution fixed for cross-file/explicit cases. Degrades gracefully (an `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT` diagnostic on that one field, not a crash or component loss).

109	8. **`update_file`'s `changed` path must be canonicalized the same way `discover_files` canonicalizes at cold-start.** `discover_files` resolves symlinks (e.g. macOS's `/var` → `/private/var`), so every file key and recorded dependency is in that form. A raw watcher path that skips `canonicalize_best_effort` matches no dependency and silently under-updates.
110	
111	## Locked design decisions
112	
113	- **Parallel discovery, parse and resolve; everything else sequential.** Already covered above under "the 6-phase data flow" — restated here because it's the decision most likely to look "obviously improvable" by parallelizing merge/collect too. Don't: both are cheap relative to parse/resolve, and both build one shared mutable structure whose synchronization cost would exceed the sequential cost.
114	- **The DTS cache keys each entry on `(path, content hash)` and the whole cache on the build that wrote it.** The payload's header (schema version, crate version, source fingerprint from `build.rs`) must match the running build, or the cache is discarded (ADR 0008). `stats.dtsFilesParsed` and `stats.dtsCacheHits` come from the cache's own counters, so the TypeScript lib files merged in Phase 3.6 count too.
115	- **`contain_panic` uses `AssertUnwindSafe` internally, not at call sites.** Plugin hooks pass `&mut SourceData`/`&mut ComponentEntry`, and `&mut T` is unconditionally `!UnwindSafe` in std — requiring callers to prove unwind-safety themselves would make every call site either not compile or need its own `AssertUnwindSafe`. The justification is structural, not incidental: `SourceData`/`ComponentEntry` have no interior mutability (`Cell`/`RefCell`), so a caught panic mid-operation can't leave an observably-torn half-write behind — the whole operation's output is simply discarded. See ADR 0005 and `panic_guard.rs:14-19`.

1	# Performance
2	
3	How fast Caliper is and what it costs is recorded in `docs/measurement.md`: a weekly run on five pinned corpora, and `just bench` for a change that touches the resolver. The criterion benches (`cargo bench -p caliper-docgen-core`) and `docs/benchmarks.md` cover single fixtures. This page keeps the measurements that explain where the time goes.
4	
5	The per-pull-request scorecard that used to enforce these numbers is gone. It caught one real regression (Mantine 38% and Chakra 47% slower after a batch of 20 resolver pull requests merged on 2026-10-26, found by the weekly run), and its gates failed on runner noise and on bases that had moved. The figures below came from it and are history, not limits.
6	
7	## Size model
8	
9	Extraction time fits t ≈ 6.4 ms + 0.13 ms/kLOC + 3.8 ms/kprop (props summed over components). It is a sizing guide, reported by the old scorecard as "Model ms", never a gate: a fixed cost that varies by machine dominates small corpora, so per-corpus residuals vary too much to gate on. On the run below the model is within 2× of the measured extract time on every corpus (0.45× for mantine to 1.6× for chakra).
10	
11	## Results, 2026-10-22
12	
13	Apple Silicon laptop, macOS, load average 8 to 12, 10 runs per corpus, branch `ci/size-normalized-gates`.
14

# Performance

How fast Caliper is and what it costs is recorded in `docs/measurement.md`: a weekly run on five pinned corpora, and `just bench` for a change that touches the resolver. The criterion benches (`cargo bench -p caliper-docgen-core`) and `docs/benchmarks.md` cover single fixtures. This page keeps the measurements that explain where the time goes.

The per-pull-request scorecard that used to enforce these numbers is gone. It caught one real regression (Mantine 38% and Chakra 47% slower after a batch of 20 resolver pull requests merged on 2026-10-26, found by the weekly run), and its gates failed on runner noise and on bases that had moved. The figures below came from it and are history, not limits.

## Size model

Extraction time fits t ≈ 6.4 ms + 0.13 ms/kLOC + 3.8 ms/kprop (props summed over components). It is a sizing guide, reported by the old scorecard as "Model ms", never a gate: a fixed cost that varies by machine dominates small corpora, so per-corpus residuals vary too much to gate on. On the run below the model is within 2× of the measured extract time on every corpus (0.45× for mantine to 1.6× for chakra).

## Results, 2026-10-22

Apple Silicon laptop, macOS, load average 8 to 12, 10 runs per corpus, branch `ci/size-normalized-gates`.

| Corpus | kLOC | Components | Props | Unresolved | Wall ms | Extract ms | Peak RSS MB | Model ms | RDT ms | vs RDT |
| --- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| mantine | 79.6 | 355 | 19,763 | 146 | 63.6 | 41.5 | 153 | 92 | 1,263 | 20× |
| chakra | 40.8 | 600 | 560 | 403 | 33.6 | 23.0 | 66 | 14 | 1,321 | 39× |
| shadcn | 489.6 | 2,140 | 1,615 | 1,526 | 80.1 | 64.0 | 104 | 76 | 1,906 | 24× |
| antd | 172.4 | 365 | 3,514 | 316 | 61.3 | 48.0 | 87 | 42 | 1,014 | 17× |
| spectrum | 256.6 | 1,482 | 7,031 | 1,901 | 80.9 | 60.0 | 116 | 66 | 1,787 | 22× |

Scaling: one copy of mantine 26 ms, two copies 46 ms (1.77×).

RDT's component and prop counts are not comparable with Caliper's here: without dependencies it reports every exported function and expands what it can of `@types/react`. Precision is in `docs/precision.md`; recall and agreement with RDT on installed repos, gated weekly, are in `docs/parity.md`.

## Dependency loading against RDT, 2026-10-23

Whether `--load-dependencies` can become the default (ADR 0010). The five repos with their dependencies installed, RDT run on the same component files through each repo's sources (`skipLibCheck`, dependencies resolvable), Caliper in RDT's format with `--html-attributes full`. The 20 fixture libraries can't answer this: they are single copied files with no installed packages.

## Chained lazy dependency layers, 2026-10-25

On the five installed parity corpora, `lazy_bench` with dependency loading and full HTML attributes, best of three runs per scenario. `random50` asks 50 seeded components one at a time; `all` asks every listed component in key order. Peak RSS is per process. The comparison uses the same build with the whole-demand threshold at three or 48 growths; this change sets the threshold to three (design in `docs/architecture/pipeline-orchestration.md`, "Demand-driven dependencies").

| Corpus   | 50 requests: 3 → 48 growths | Peak MB: 3 → 48 | All requests: 3 → 48 | Peak MB: 3 → 48 |
| -------- | --------------------------: | --------------: | -------------------: | --------------: |
| Mantine  |                  30 → 27 ms |         68 → 67 |         163 → 170 ms |         88 → 84 |
| Chakra   |                234 → 271 ms |       107 → 105 |     2,117 → 2,384 ms |       317 → 317 |
| shadcn   |                  52 → 72 ms |        144 → 94 |         213 → 272 ms |       159 → 159 |
| antd     |                  18 → 46 ms |         71 → 73 |          56 → 126 ms |         81 → 84 |
| Spectrum |                  20 → 47 ms |        102 → 90 |         162 → 222 ms |       134 → 134 |

All ten output digests match across thresholds and the pre-chain build. The three-growth chain is also faster than the pre-chain three-growth build on 50 requests for all five corpora: 42 → 30 ms on Mantine, 313 → 234 on Chakra, 61 → 52 on shadcn, 23 → 18 on antd, and 27 → 20 on Spectrum. A file first parsed as a re-export stub must be indexed when later claimed; without that step, 28 shadcn components lost props in the whole-project run. The regression test and forward-order corpus parity check cover it.

    ("Version 3 (ADR 0023) adds `optional` and `rest` to a function type's parameters, written only when true, and lists a rest parameter as the last parameter.",
     "Version 3 adds `optional` and `rest` to a function type's parameters, written only when true, and lists a rest parameter as the last parameter. OXC keeps `...rest` apart from the other parameters and the extractor read only the others, so `(...args: any[]) => void` printed as `() => void` and `(a?: string) => void` as `(a: string) => void`; a caller reading the signature believed an argument was required or that none were accepted. It is a bump, not an addition a reader can ignore: a version 2 reader would show `...args: any[]` as a required parameter named `args`. The Vite plugin and the Storybook addon read version 3 only, and an old parse cache is discarded once. `raw_string` prints `a?: T` and `...a: T[]` as RDT does, TOON prints `T?` and `...T`, and `structural_hash` includes both flags. The TypeScript 7.1 backend does not set them: `crates/semantic/src/convert.rs` builds every parameter as required. Not carried yet, and best landed together as one more bump: `readonly` (the extractor peels it from `readonly string[]` on purpose; carrying it needs a flag on `PropType::Array` and `Tuple`, their collected forms, the union normalizer, the evaluator's assignability and every printer) and `RefObject` (`resolver/react.rs` maps `Ref`, `RefObject`, `ForwardedRef`, `MutableRefObject`, `RefCallback` and `LegacyRef` to one `PropType::Ref { element }`)."),
])

edit("docs/rdt-coverage.md", [
    ("- **Full (default)** —",
     "- **Full (default since 2026-10-26)** —"),
    ("- **None** — no inherited HTML attributes synthesized at all; own props only.\n",
     "- **None** — no inherited HTML attributes synthesized at all; own props only.\n\n"
     "**Why `full` is the default.** `curated` was meant to keep the props table short, but it left props React declares out of the answer: `--format rdt` and the addon's `docgenInfo` never emitted `notableInherited`, so no handler of a curated component reached Storybook, and a props type that reached an element through `Omit<HTMLAttributes<…>>`, `ComponentProps<\"div\">` or `PropsWithoutRef<…>` had no element layer in `full` either (antd's `PurePanel`, `Dragger`'s `capture`, `ref` on `forwardRef` components). The addon's `collapseInheritedProps` already hides props inherited from dependencies, so a long list does not make the UI long. `skipHtmlProps` still means `none`; `key` is omitted in every mode; `ref` is listed for `ComponentProps<\"div\">` props and `forwardRef` components. Without `@types/react`, `full` lists no inherited attributes and reports one info diagnostic per component that needed them. Cost against the old default and Storybook parity numbers: `docs/performance.md`, \"Default changes\".\n\n"
     "**Curated reads React apart.** When two members of an intersection declare the same prop, TypeScript intersects both types, and an HTML layer such as `ComponentProps<\"div\">` declares every attribute of its element without listing them, so a library prop named like a DOM attribute (recharts' `onTimeUpdate`) has the attribute's type as well. In curated mode the cold run parses `@types/react` (through the parse cache) into its own `NamedTypeIndex`, held by the revision and passed to `ResolutionContext::with_react_types`. Only the HTML-layer attribute lookup (`resolver/html.rs`, `ResolutionContext::react_index`) and member reads through React's types read it; it is not a fallback of the project index, because merging React into it would resolve every other React name in curated output (`ReactNode`, `CSSProperties`, the handler aliases) against the real declarations and change far more than these collisions. `full` merges React into the project index; `none` and the dependency loader do not read React at all. A colliding prop has both types in curated mode too, with both declarations listed, and the attribute keeps its alias name (`ReactEventHandler<HTMLDivElement>`). Without `@types/react`, curated behaves as it did and reports nothing.\n"),
])

with open(ROOT + "docs/performance.md", "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write("""
## Default changes

Two defaults flipped after measurement. Both tables are history, not limits.

### Dependency loading on, 2026-10-25

`PipelineOptions::load_dependencies` defaults to `true` (the CLI, the config file, the Vite plugin, the NAPI binding and the addon; the addon already did). `--no-load-dependencies` turns it off, `--load-dependencies` still means the default, and a project with no packages installed loads nothing either way. It was off while Chakra took 497 ms and 1.3 GB with it on, against 43 ms and 82 MiB without; memo replay, `keyof` name walks, interned keys and a parallel lib parse (#136, #175, #177, #178, #182) took that to about 220 ms and 330 MiB. Five parity corpora, `extract --json`, best of 7, interleaved, on a laptop shared with other jobs (about ±10 ms), off → on:

| Corpus   |  Wall ms | Peak RSS MiB |           Props | Unresolved warnings |
| -------- | -------: | -----------: | --------------: | ------------------: |
| mantine  |  50 → 60 |    112 → 128 | 19,834 → 19,834 |             14 → 10 |
| chakra   | 50 → 220 |    101 → 330 |   592 → 479,235 |             315 → 0 |
| shadcn   |  50 → 90 |    101 → 225 |   1,543 → 8,131 |           816 → 190 |
| antd     |  40 → 50 |     95 → 114 |   3,349 → 3,856 |              76 → 8 |
| spectrum |  70 → 90 |    136 → 161 | 32,585 → 32,587 |              13 → 5 |

Output is exact: the new default is byte-identical to the previous build's `--load-dependencies` output, and `--no-load-dependencies` to the previous default. Share of react-docgen-typescript's props reported, off → on (the 0.4.0 baseline, since removed): Chakra 0.1% → 98.6%, shadcn 6.4% → 39.5%, antd 71.8% → 80.3%, Mantine and Spectrum 99.7% both. The cost lands on a few projects: Chakra is 4.4× slower and holds 3.3× the memory, shadcn takes 40 ms and 124 MiB more, the others 10 to 20 ms and 16 to 25 MiB. A CI job that needs the old speed passes `--no-load-dependencies`.

### Every HTML attribute listed, 2026-10-26

`PipelineOptions::html_attributes` defaults to `full` (the reasons are in `docs/rdt-coverage.md`, HtmlAttributeMode). Five parity corpora with dependencies loaded, canonical JSON, no cache, median of 11 (wall) and 21 (CPU, peak RSS), old default (`curated` at 338d1ddc) → new default:

| Corpus   |   Wall ms |       CPU s | Peak RSS MiB |     JSON MB |
| -------- | --------: | ----------: | -----------: | ----------: |
| antd     |   56 → 62 | 0.33 → 0.37 |    130 → 151 |   3.6 → 6.3 |
| chakra   | 424 → 470 | 3.13 → 3.72 |    514 → 577 | 11.1 → 16.7 |
| mantine  | 149 → 164 | 1.05 → 1.21 |    175 → 229 |  8.4 → 14.2 |
| spectrum |   90 → 98 | 0.68 → 0.73 |    171 → 191 |  8.3 → 11.7 |
| shadcn   | 144 → 188 | 1.28 → 1.72 |    220 → 301 |  5.9 → 12.2 |

The default is slower and larger than the old one at that commit: wall time +9 to +31%, peak RSS +12 to +37%, canonical JSON +42 to +105%. Most of the wall time was a lookup bug, fixed in #241 (indexing component lookups by name): shadcn `full` went from 153 to 127 ms, against 124 ms for the old default, with identical output. On the Storybook request path the first story was no slower with `full` than with `none`. Storybook parity (props Storybook lists that the addon lacks, antd / shadcn / Spectrum): 37 / 0 / 1 → 34 / 0 / 1. `ref` on `forwardRef` components written as `React.forwardRef(Inner)` is listed since #244; `PurePanel`'s 33 props, Drawer's own, remain because the declared type does not extend them.
""")

1	# Architecture
2	
3	This is the entry point: the pipeline shape, the crate graph, the key types, and why the big calls were made. For subsystem-level detail — invariants, locked design decisions, known gaps, each checked against the real source — see `docs/architecture/`, starting at `docs/architecture/README.md`'s task-to-file routing table.
4	
5	## Pipeline
6	
7	Every extraction — cold or incremental — flows through four phases:
8	
9	```mermaid
10	flowchart LR
11	    src["Source files\n.ts / .tsx / .d.ts"]
12	    oxc["OXC parser\none allocator per file"]
13	    sd["SourceData\ninterfaces, type aliases,\nimport bindings, defaults"]
14	    gsd["GlobalSourceData\nmerged across all files\nArc<ArcSwap<…>>"]
15	    ce["ComponentEntry\nresolved props,\ninheritance chain"]
16	    out["ExtractionOutput\nJSON-serializable"]
17	
18	    src -->|"discover_files()\nignore crate"| oxc

# Architecture

This is the entry point: the pipeline shape, the crate graph, the key types, and why the big calls were made. For subsystem-level detail — invariants, locked design decisions, known gaps, each checked against the real source — see `docs/architecture/`, starting at `docs/architecture/README.md`'s task-to-file routing table.

## Pipeline

Every extraction — cold or incremental — flows through four phases:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    src["Source files\n.ts / .tsx / .d.ts"]
    oxc["OXC parser\none allocator per file"]
    sd["SourceData\ninterfaces, type aliases,\nimport bindings, defaults"]
    gsd["GlobalSourceData\nmerged across all files\nArc<ArcSwap<…>>"]
    ce["ComponentEntry\nresolved props,\ninheritance chain"]
    out["ExtractionOutput\nJSON-serializable"]

    src -->|"discover_files()\nignore crate"| oxc
    oxc -->|"parse_file()\nper-file parallel"| sd
    sd -->|"rayon par_iter\nmerge()"| gsd
    gsd -->|"resolve_component()\nper-component parallel"| ce
    ce -->|"pipeline::extract()"| out
```

Each `parse_file()` call gets its own OXC allocator. No AST node escapes the function — all extracted data is owned, heap-allocated types. This is what makes the rayon parallelism safe.

The watch path reuses analysis across file changes. A single-file update calls `parse_file()` on the changed file and re-resolves only the affected components.

`WatchSession` publishes one immutable `Revision` at a time: global source data, the named-type index, resolved components with their recorded dependencies, diagnostics and the assembled output. An update builds the next revision off to the side and publishes it with one atomic store, so a reader sees one complete revision. Cold extraction and watch revisions share `Revision::assemble()`, and a watch snapshot equals a cold extract of the same files (see `docs/architecture/pipeline-orchestration.md`).

## Crate and package graph

```mermaid
graph TD
    core["crates/core\ncaliper-docgen-core\nPure extraction — no I/O, no async"]
    binding["crates/binding\ncaliper-docgen-napi\nNAPI + tokio runtime"]
    cli["crates/cli\ncaliper-docgen\nCLI binary"]
    napi["packages/napi\ncaliper-docgen-napi\nTS types + dev binary loader"]
    vite["packages/vite-plugin\ncaliper-docgen-vite-plugin\nVite HMR plugin"]
    storybook["packages/storybook\ncaliper-docgen-storybook\nStorybook 11 docgen provider"]
    validate["apps/validate\nAccuracy comparison harness"]

    core --> binding
    core --> cli
    binding --> napi
    napi --> vite
    napi --> storybook
    cli -.->|"runtime dep"| validate
    napi -.->|"runtime dep"| validate
```

`crates/core` has no dependency on async runtimes, NAPI, or terminal libraries. It can be linked from any host.

## Module layout

### `crates/core/src/`

```
types/
  collected.rs    — CollectedType, SourceData, RawProp, ImportBinding, LexedExport
  output.rs       — PropType, ComponentEntry, ExtractionOutput, InheritedLayer, ParsedProp
  diagnostic.rs   — Diagnostic, DiagnosticSeverity, DiagnosticCode
  global.rs       — GlobalSourceData, ScopedKey

extractor/
  mod.rs          — parse_file() entry point; SourceDataCollector struct
  visit.rs        — impl Visit for SourceDataCollector (AST walker)
  component.rs    — component pattern detection (FC, forwardRef, HOC, exotic)
  interface.rs    — collect_interface, collect_raw_props, collect_object_fields
  alias.rs        — classify_type_alias (Omit/Pick/Passthrough/Union/Intersection)
  jsdoc.rs        — find_jsdoc, extract_jsdoc_tags, parse_jsdoc_text
  defaults.rs     — extract_param_defaults from destructured function parameters

resolver/
  mod.rs          — resolve_component(); ResolutionContext; ResolveState (per-call)
  chain.rs        — resolve_props_chain, resolve_interface_chain
  extends.rs      — resolve_extends_ref
  alias.rs        — resolve_type_alias_chain, resolve_base_as_chain
  primitives.rs   — resolve_union, resolve_intersection, resolve_indexed_access
  collected.rs    — CollectedType → PropType dispatch
  named.rs        — resolve_named (main named-type lookup and import following)
  template.rs     — resolve_template_literal
  func.rs         — resolve_function_type, resolve_typeof
  import.rs       — resolve_to_canonical, resolve_import_specifier
  html.rs         — infer_html_attr_prop_type
  react.rs        — react_type_to_prop_type

pipeline/
  mod.rs          — extract(); PipelineOptions; resolution orchestration
  discover.rs     — discover_files (directory walk + gitignore via ignore crate)
  revision.rs     — Revision: cold build, incremental next(), assemble() shared by both
  watch.rs        — WatchSession: publishes one Revision at a time

known.rs          — library shortcuts: SxProps, VariantProps, sx, css, cva, tv, defineRecipe…
react_types.rs    — React builtin recognition + notable HTML attribute table
import_map.rs     — import binding resolution
cache.rs          — DTS parse cache (mtime + size invalidation, msgpack, atomic write)
```

### `crates/cli/src/`

```
main.rs           — Cli struct, Command enum, main(), init_tracing()
config.rs         — docgen.config.ts loading via node+tsx (result discarded; next milestone)
output.rs         — print_summary, print_diagnostics, comfy-table helpers
commands/
  extract.rs      — cmd_extract (RDT / Storybook output)
  watch.rs        — cmd_watch (watchexec integration)
  inspect.rs      — cmd_inspect (single-file table view)
  check.rs        — cmd_check
  completions.rs  — shell completion generation
```

## Key types

### `CollectedType` — raw structural type from the extractor

The AST visitor produces `CollectedType` without doing any semantic resolution. It describes the structure of a TypeScript type as written, not what it means.

```
Named { name: "ButtonVariants", args: [] }
Union([Named { name: "string" }, Named { name: "undefined" }])
Intersection([Named { name: "ButtonHTMLAttributes", args: ["button"] }, Object([…])])
Omit { base: Named { name: "InputProps" }, keys: ["value"] }
```

### `PropType` — resolved semantic type for consumers

The resolver transforms `CollectedType` into `PropType`. This is the discriminated union that appears in `ExtractionOutput` and the TypeScript types package.

```
{ kind: "literalUnion", members: ["default", "destructive", "outline"], hasDefault: true }
{ kind: "eventHandler", eventType: "MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>" }
{ kind: "htmlAttributes", element: "button", omitted: [] }
{ kind: "opaque", raw: "ConditionalType<…>", reason: { type: "conditionalType" } }
```

### `ResolveState`

Created fresh for each `resolve_component()` call. Holds:

- Visited-type set for cycle detection (`FxHashSet<CompactString>`)
- Current recursion depth
- Accumulated diagnostics

Not shared between threads — rayon creates one per component.

### `GlobalSourceData`

The merged view across all parsed files: component declarations, type aliases, interface definitions, import bindings. Today `WatchSession` publishes this map independently via `ArcSwap`. Under the target watch invariant above it becomes one member of the immutable aggregate `WatchRevision`, so readers load one coherent published revision.

## Design decisions

### OXC instead of the TypeScript compiler

`react-docgen-typescript` creates a TypeScript `Program` — this loads all imported types transitively, runs type inference, and is single-threaded. `caliper-docgen` parses each file independently in parallel with no type-checking pass. The trade-off: TypeScript-only semantics (conditional types, `infer`, deep utility type evaluation) fall through to `{ kind: "opaque" }`. Everything structurally expressible — interfaces, intersections, unions, `Omit`, `Pick`, `VariantProps` — resolves correctly.

### `FxHashMap` over `HashMap`

OXC uses `FxHashMap` throughout. For short keys (type names, file paths) the FNV-derived hash in `rustc-hash` is faster than SipHash with no DoS-relevant surface for this use case.

### `CompactString` for type and prop names

Most names in the hot path (`string`, `boolean`, `ReactNode`, `MouseEvent`, `className`) are ≤24 bytes. `CompactString` stores them inline without heap allocation. Extraction visits thousands of names per file; this adds up.

### Manual `Serialize`/`Deserialize` for `CollectedType` and `PropType`

Both are deeply recursive enums. `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]` hit Rust's monomorphization recursion limit during macro expansion, producing 19-minute compile times. Both now implement serialization manually through `serde_json::Value` as an intermediate, which breaks the recursion chain at the cost of one heap allocation per serialized value. A `#![recursion_limit = "2048"]` attribute is still present in `lib.rs` for other traits but is no longer load-bearing for these types.

### DTS cache location: `node_modules/.cache/`

`.d.ts` files from `node_modules` rarely change within a project session. The cache stores parsed `SourceData` keyed by file path, mtime, and size, serialized with msgpack and written atomically. `node_modules/.cache/` is the correct location: it is cleaned with `node_modules`, excluded from version control, and preserved across CI runs when `node_modules` is cached by layer.

### `hotUpdate` returns `undefined`, not `[]`

Vite's `hotUpdate` hook suppresses React Fast Refresh for a changed file if any plugin returns `[]` (empty module list). The plugin returns `undefined` to let both paths run: our metadata update fires, and React's HMR still re-renders the component. Returning `[]` is the more common pattern and the wrong one here.

### `BTreeMap` for JSON output maps

Component props and enums are serialized as `BTreeMap<String, …>` rather than `FxHashMap`. This gives stable key ordering across runs — important for snapshot tests, diffs, and downstream tools that consume the JSON.

## What is not yet implemented

| Feature | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Preset system (`caliper-docgen-presets`) | Designed; no Rust changes needed — config-side only. |
| Conditional types (`T extends U ? X : Y`) | Emitted as `opaque` — needs a real type checker, see `docs/type-checker-integration.md`. |
| Mapped types with computed keys | Emitted as `opaque`. |

 # Entire repository agent guide — Brain
 
-Use Brain for task context and retained knowledge. Begin substantive tasks needing
-orientation with:
+Use Brain for task context and retained knowledge. Begin substantive tasks needing orientation with:
 
     entire brain brief "<task>" --json
 
-Run it before deciding the task does not need it: what the brief adds is the part
-you do not already know about.
+Run it before deciding the task does not need it: what the brief adds is the part you do not already know about.
 
-Questions about why something is the way it is, what was decided, or what was
-tried before are answered by durable memories. Retrieve them directly; the brief's
-memories section is a sample, not the search:
+Questions about why something is the way it is, what was decided, or what was tried before are answered by durable memories. Retrieve them directly; the brief's memories section is a sample, not the search:
 
     entire brain recall "<question>" --json
 
-recall ranks decisions, rejected approaches, invariants and gotchas first. query
-mixes memories with history and documentation and can rank documentation above the
-recorded decision.
+recall ranks decisions, rejected approaches, invariants and gotchas first. query mixes memories with history and documentation and can rank documentation above the recorded decision.
 
-Reuse useful code locations from the brief. Use Brain retrieval for previous
-decisions, attempts, documentation, and durable memories - Brain's episodic record
-of what was decided, what went wrong before, and what must stay true. Record one
-when you learn something durable that the code does not already state:
+Reuse useful code locations from the brief. Use Brain retrieval for previous decisions, attempts, documentation, and durable memories - Brain's episodic record of what was decided, what went wrong before, and what must stay true. Record one when you learn something durable that the code does not already state:
 
     entire brain remember "<memory>" --path <category.subcategory.type> --json
 
-Categories are architecture, constraints, preferences, project and workflow.
-Omitting --path classifies the memory for you, which requires a supported coding
-agent on PATH. Over MCP the same write is the brain_remember tool, which
-requires path. Retrieve with recall, and re-check anchors with verify.
+Categories are architecture, constraints, preferences, project and workflow. Omitting --path classifies the memory for you, which requires a supported coding agent on PATH. Over MCP the same write is the brain_remember tool, which requires path. Retrieve with recall, and re-check anchors with verify.
 
-Use Brain entities history to connect code changes to earlier checkpoints and
-sessions. Use Brain memory-informed review and workspace
-capabilities when relevant. Brain semantic answers refer to a stored index, which
-may differ from current working-tree source.
+Use Brain entities history to connect code changes to earlier checkpoints and sessions. Use Brain memory-informed review and workspace capabilities when relevant. Brain semantic answers refer to a stored index, which may differ from current working-tree source.
 
 Use Brain's code inspection tools for relevant code questions.
 
-Read focused source around useful locations before editing. Check related contracts
-and make the smallest complete change. VERIFY before stopping: execute focused tests,
-a reproduction, or the most relevant build. If execution is unavailable, disclose
-that limit and perform a bounded source check. Prefer precise queries and line ranges,
-but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
-
-Current source and executed tests establish present behavior. Historical memory
-explains prior intent or behavior. Investigate disagreements.

## Releases

Add a changeset for a consumer-visible change (`.changeset/`; see `AGENTS.md` for how to write one). Callisto 0.16 plans the versions from the changesets and opens a release pull request (`callisto/version-packages`); merging it runs `.github/workflows/release.yml`, which publishes the crates and npm packages and tags the CLI release `npm/caliper-docgen@x.y.z`.

Homebrew pulls from us: the tap's daily `brew bump` finds that tag with `livecheck`, builds `crates/cli` from source and bottles it, and a maintainer merges the formula pull request. Nothing in this repository notifies the tap.

Speed, memory and accuracy are recorded weekly and compared with the previous run (`docs/measurement.md`); there is no pull-request gate. Run `just bench` when a change touches the resolver.

## Pull requests

1. Branch from `main`
2. Keep the pre-commit hook passing
3. Update snapshots if extraction output changes (`cargo insta review`)
4. One logical change per PR — squash fixup commits before merging

> `moon run validate:compare` is a developer tool for checking accuracy against real libraries. It exits 0 regardless of coverage gaps and is not a CI gate.

content.content:
# Dependency updates. Every ecosystem is grouped into a single routine PR per
# week so the queue stays reviewable, with security updates kept in their own
# group so an advisory fix is never hidden inside a large routine bump.
#
# `cooldown` deliberately lags fresh releases: this repo pins GitHub Actions
# by commit SHA, and a week is long enough for a yanked crate or a pulled
# action release to surface before it lands in a PR here.
version: 2

updates:
  - package-ecosystem: github-actions
    directory: /
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
    cooldown:
      default-days: 7
    open-pull-requests-limit: 3
    groups:
      routine-actions:
        applies-to: version-updates
        patterns: ["*"]
      security-actions:
        applies-to: security-updates
        patterns: ["*"]

  - package-ecosystem: cargo
    directory: /
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
    cooldown:
      default-days: 7
    open-pull-requests-limit: 5
    groups:
      # oxc_resolver is versioned separately from the lockstep oxc_* crates, so it gets its own PR.
      oxc-resolver:
        applies-to: version-updates
        patterns: ["oxc_resolver"]
      # The oxc_* crates are released in lockstep and their minor releases
      # carry breaking API changes; keeping them in one PR means the
      # extractor and resolver are updated together or not at all.
      oxc:
        applies-to: version-updates
        patterns: ["oxc_*"]
        exclude-patterns: ["oxc_resolver"]
      routine-cargo:
        applies-to: version-updates
        patterns: ["*"]
        exclude-patterns: ["oxc_*"]
      security-cargo:
        applies-to: security-updates
        patterns: ["*"]

  - package-ecosystem: npm
    directory: /
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
    cooldown:
      default-days: 7
    open-pull-requests-limit: 3
    groups:
      routine-npm:
        applies-to: version-updates
        patterns: ["*"]
      security-npm:
        applies-to: security-updates
        patterns: ["*"]

input.content:
ADRs are for architecture: a boundary, a data contract, a dependency or technology choice, or a cross-cutting constraint, and expensive to reverse. This retires the nine that recorded a default, a lookup order, a tuning or a procedure, moves their why and measurements into the pages that own them, and brings the docs in line with the code. Part of trail #88.

**Stacked on #259** (the lint fix: `main` has been red since #257). Merge #259 first; GitHub retargets this to `main`.

## ADRs

| ADR | Verdict | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 OXC | keep | The technology choice behind the whole pipeline |
| 2 manual `Serialize` for `PropType` | keep | A hidden constraint on a data contract |
| 3 positional msgpack cache | keep | A data contract that fails silently when broken |
| 5 panic containment | keep | A cross-cutting boundary |
| 6, 7 semantic backend | keep | A second resolver, compiled in, runtime opt-in |
| 9, 18 canonical output interns props, prop sets and name lists | keep | The shape of the canonical JSON; 9's key is in the published schema's descriptions |
| 10 load dependency declarations by name | keep | How dependency types reach the resolver |
| 16 resolve on request | keep | A structural change to sessions |
| 17 version the canonical JSON | keep | A contract rule |
| 22 ask a warm checker | keep | Routes the backend through a session |
| 8 parse cache keyed by build | retire | The invalidation policy of one cache. Now in `pipeline-orchestration.md` |
| 11 per-package export index | retire | How one module stores what it loaded. Now in `resolver-type-resolution.md` |
| 12 collapse large dependency sources | retire | A default and a threshold. Now in `resolver-type-resolution.md` |
| 13 curated reads React apart | retire | A resolver behavior of an opt-in mode. Now in `rdt-coverage.md` |
| 14 declarations before shortcuts | retire | A lookup order. Now in `resolver-type-resolution.md` |
| 19 load dependencies by default | retire | A default. Measurements now in `performance.md` |
| 21 publish the semantic crates | retire | A release procedure; Callisto orders the publish |
| 23 function parameters carry `optional` and `rest` | retire | A field added under 17's rule. Now in `serialization-formats.md` |
| 24 list every HTML attribute by default | retire | A default. Now in `rdt-coverage.md` and `performance.md` |

Retired numbers stay in `docs/adr/README.md` as one-line tombstones, with a "not ADR material" rule for fields added under 0017 and for defaults flipped after a measurement. Code comments that cited a retired ADR now name the rule ("precedence", "collapse", "persisted index", "React index"), each a heading in the page that holds it.

## Docs

- `STATUS.md`: date; gates replaced by the weekly record; the oracle method; lazy sessions, dependency loading and TS 7.1 on-demand (default `semanticWaitMs` 150, pinned `7.1.0-beta`).
- `ARCHITECTURE.md`: the `semantic` and `tsc-client` crates and their edges, the real module layout, content-hash cache keys, dependencies loaded by default.
- `napi-binding.md`: the three entry points the page missed (`initialize_session_index`, `session_component_answers`, `session_warm_up`).
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: the NAPI list, signed commits required on `main`, and a Releases section (Callisto 0.16, the CLI tag, the pull-based Homebrew flow, no PR gate).
- `performance.md`: a "Default changes" section holding the dependency-loading and `full` tables, with #241's fix noted. It also drops a link to `docs/parity.md`, which #256 deleted.
- `rdt-coverage.md`: why `full` is the default, and how curated reads React.

## Not touched

`docs/benchmarks.md` and `docs/type-checker-integration.md` belong to #260 (`apps/oracle`), and so does `apps/validate/src/run-ours.ts`, which still cites ADR 0019 in a comment and goes away there. #260's trial merge with this branch is clean.

`just lint`, `just doc-check`, `just typos` and `cargo test -p caliper-docgen-core --no-run` pass. Only comments changed in Rust, so no changeset.
